#1926. Mauricio Pochettino's plan of action 'revealed' as new Man United manager's assistants head to Manchester to begin preparations for Liverpool

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 18:07, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 18:11

Mauricio Pochettino will reportedly be ready to start work as Manchester United head coach on Wednesday morning, with the Red Devils arranging a private jet for the Argentine to head to England once his duties with the USA have concluded.

Man United appointed Pochettino as their new head coach on Friday, but he has not yet arrived in Manchester, having agreed to take charge of USA's two matches during this international period against Haiti.

The United States beat Haiti 6-0 in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final on November 14, with the second leg taking place at midnight on Tuesday UK time.

According to the Daily Mail, Man United have arranged a private jet which will see Pochettino land in England on Wednesday morning ready to begin work.

The report claims that the 54-year-old will speak to the media and then say goodbye to his players before heading to Manchester; he will therefore sleep on the plane and be ready to head straight to Carrington to begin work.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino have already travelled to Manchester.

First-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and fitness coach Silvia Tuya are set to follow.

"The assistants are ahead. After the game they flew to Manchester and they are there in advance," Pochettino told reporters on Monday.

"That was the plan when we agreed terms with Manchester United and with the national team. They are there in advance. They are preparing because Wednesday when we will arrive it’s going to be non-stop, and then start with playing games."

Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions will be Sunday's Premier League clash against Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United will then head to Portugal at the start of next week to prepare for their Champions League contest with Sporting Lisbon on November 25.

Pochettino is expected to speak to the media at Carrington on Friday afternoon, where he will also be asked for a team news update ahead of the game with Liverpool.

#1925. Former SPFL starlet’s wonder strike seals stunning promotion with ex-Rangers icon in the dugout

Former Airdrieonians midfielder Justin Devenny was the hero for Northern Ireland as his wonder strike in the 1-1 draw with Hungary sealed their shock promotion to League A of the Nations League at the Puskas Arena.

Managed on the touchline by former Rangers hero Steven Davis in Budapest, the 41-year-old stepped into the head coach role on a crucial night for Northern Ireland, with manager Michael O’Neill suspended and forced to watch from the stands.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Promoted to League B during their last Nations League campaign, Northern Ireland entered Tuesday night’s game in remarkable form. Top of the group ahead of kick-off, they’d won three and drawn two, without conceding a single goal.

Requiring just a draw against Hungary to seal back-to-back Nations League promotion, they came under heavy pressure in the opening stages, with the home side finally breaking Northern Ireland’s resistance in the 35th minute when Barnabas Varga capitalised on a mistake from Trai Hume to place beyond Pierce Charles as the visitors conceded for the first time in 500 minutes.

Northern Ireland players vigorously appealed for a penalty after Ciaron Brown went down under a challenge from Andras Schafer in the area in the build-up to the goal, with Hungary’s subsequent clearance directly leading to Varga’s opener. However, referee Marco Guida waved away protests following a VAR check.

Searching for the goal that would secure a first promotion to League A, Northern Ireland battled back after the restart and thought they’d levelled when Isaac Price cannoned a long-range effort off the post just after the hour mark.

They found their equaliser shortly afterwards, though, and it was definitely worth the wait. A long throw from Sunderland defender Hume was half-cleared by the Hungarian defence before falling to Devenny, who took a deft first touch to control the ball, before flicking it up and blasting a volley into the top corner.

Despite being born in Irvine, the 23-year-old is eligible to play for Northern Ireland due to his grandparents. Devenny told the Belfast Telegraph that he opted to represent Northern Ireland after they approached him first and showed genuine faith in his abilities before Scotland did. During the interview, he emphasized that he chose to play for the nation he felt actively wanted him.

He began his career in the Kilmarnock youth system and spent time on loan with Broomhill and Airdrieonians before signing for the Diamonds on a permanent deal in the summer of 2022. His impressive form in the Scottish Championship won him a shock move to the English Premier League with Crystal Palace just 12 months later.

Playing over 50 games for the Eagles, the versatile midfielder won the Conference League, the FA Cup and the Community Shield during his time at Selhurst Park, before moving to EFL Championship side Stoke City for an undisclosed fee on deadline day. Scoring a brace on his debut for the club in a 4–0 win over Charlton Athletic, he’s been a regular for the Potters as they chase promotion to the top flight.

#1924. Why Man United staff feel treatment of Michael Carrick was 'disgusting' and the comment from Omar Berrada that raised eyebrows as club legend is put out of his misery - and Mauricio Pochettino gets set to take over

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 14:25 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:15 EST, 13 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino would have been fast asleep in his hotel room in the quirky American town of Trilith when Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox sat down with Michael Carrick at Carrington Thursday morning and confirmed the worst-kept secret in football.

It was time for Carrick to vacate the head coach’s office at Manchester United, and safe to say Pochettino will have his feet under the desk this time next week.

Carrick arrived at 7.50am but, unlike the last two days, he was no longer wearing his United training gear.

The agonising wait to be put out of his misery was over, and the club’s chief executive and director of football duly administered the last rites before Carrick left at 10.18am.

The decision was communicated to staff and Under-21s boss Adam Lawrence took training with the players who have remained at Carrington during the international break.

The first reports of Carrick’s sacking broke at 9.30am, but United insisted that they were premature and it wasn’t until 10.37am that the news was confirmed in a 142-word statement.

Michael Carrick finally left Carrington on Thursday morning after an agonising wait to be put out of his misery

Staff at Manchester United believe that the former club captain's treatment at the hands of their Ineos paymasters has been 'disgusting'

It's understood that his backroom staff - assistant Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeper coach Craig Mawson - have also gone. When Evans left on Wednesday night with his car piled high with cardboard boxes, it didn't bode well.

The treatment of Carrick and Evans, in particular, has upset staff. Two highly-respected figures at United, whose association with the club goes back more than 20 years, have been left hanging while their employers stumble over a succession plan.

Members of staff share Gary Neville’s view that Berrada and Wilcox meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, and making a move for Pochettino while Carrick had to keep driving past the cameras on his way into Carrington for the last three days, was ‘disgusting’.

It has also reignited anger over the 450 job cuts carried out by Ratcliffe and Ineos over the past three years while pouring millions down the drain in compensation.

The £10million to buy Pochettino and his staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation, and the pay-off owing to Carrick and Co, will push the cost of hiring and firing coaches in the Ineos era close to £50m.

No wonder eyebrows were raised when Berrada spoke at Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary dinner at Old Trafford on Friday night and talked about building a culture at the club.

The feeling is that changing United’s head coach won’t make a shred of difference if there isn’t significant change higher up the chain.

It has once again turned the spotlight on the relationship between Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, who from February can force him to sell his 28 per cent holding to a third party for less than the £25-per-share he paid in 2024 unless he can match the offer and buy the club himself.

However, United sources say they had little choice but to sack Carrick with the club in the relegation zone, having decided to give him a stay of execution at the end of last month.

Since then, the club had carried out a comprehensive review and come to the conclusion that a record of one win from 10 Premier League games was unacceptable.

The sources indicated that the United board shared the frustration and anger felt by fans over the situation, and believe that a change of head coach will bring about an improvement from a squad that is far better than results would suggest.

While United praised Carrick for his ‘highest degree of professionalism’, there was only silence from the players on social media.

Many of them are on international duty, including Bruno Fernandes whose criticism of Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat to Como proved so damaging.

Following the announcement of Carrick's dismissal none of his former players - including Bruno Fernandes - were quick to say their goodbyes publicly

Meanwhile, his would-be successor Mauricio Pochettino is set to face the media on Friday

Pochettino will inherit this squad of players once he has completed his duties as US national team coach with the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is due to speak at 2.15pm Friday ahead of the first leg in Miami on Saturday night when he will face questions over the United job for the first time.

Pochettino is expected to stay in charge for the second leg in Cincinnati in the early hours of Wednesday morning before flying to Manchester to meet the players and prepare for the crunch clash with Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

The US have been staying in Trilith, near their new training headquarters in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta, where they were also based before the World Cup.

It’s a unique place designed for the film industry and built around the Trilith Studios which are the largest outside Hollywood. The ideal place for Pochettino to prepare for life at Old Trafford.

He has embraced the American lifestyle since he was appointed US coach in September 2024, a few months after leaving Chelsea, and will be sorry to leave.

Pochettino is said to have developed a love of bourbon whiskey, country music and Nashville, with Ella Langley’s Choosin’ Texas one of his favourite tunes.

He has admitted crying over Miracle, the movie about the US hockey team made up of college kids famously beating the Soviet Union to the gold medal at the 1980 Winter Olympics.

But the pull of Manchester United was always going to be too great, and very soon he will be swapping Trilith for Old Trafford.

#1922. Everton transfer news: Jack Grealish replacement emerges with Toffees among ‘top contenders’ for 21 G/A winger

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 18:19

Everton have identified Flamengo winger Samuel Lino as a possible transfer target, according to a report.

The Toffees are expected to bolster their squad in the January after enduring a frustrating end to the summer transfer window, selling Iliman Ndiaye, Beto and Tim Iroegbunam on Deadline Day without bringing in a replacement.

While the addition of a new centre-forward to ease the burden on Thierno Barry is thought to be among Everton’s main priorities, pursuing a new winger may also be high on the agenda for manager David Moyes.

The long-term future of Manchester City loanee Jack Grealish has come under the spotlight following his ‘breach of club discipline’ prior to the international break.

Tyrique George has since stepped up in Grealish’s absence on the left flank, while fellow wingers Brennan Johnson and Tyler Dibling have struggled to reach the heights expected on a consistent basis for some time.

According to Swiss news outlet 4-4-2, via the Liverpool Echo, Everton are among a number of 'top contenders' in the race to sign Brazil international Lino, along with Paris Saint-Germain, Juventus and Napoli.

The report adds that Roma – who along with Everton are owned by The Friedkin Group – recently saw a €25m (£20.9m) offer for Lino rejected by Flamengo.

Lino has established himself as a prolific winger with Flamengo this season, scoring 12 goals and providing nine assists in 33 Brazilian Serie A appearances.

The 26-year-old was not called up to Brazil’s squad for the November international break, but he did represent Carlo Ancelotti’s side last month and scored his first two goals from his country in a 4-0 friendly win over India.

Lino is thriving in his homeland having previously spent five-and-a-half years in Europe with Gil Vicente, Atletico Madrid and Valencia.

After scoring 23 goals in 100 games for Portuguese side Gil Vicente, Lino made the move to Atletico in July 2022 before spending a season on loan at Valencia, chipping in with eight goals and three assists in 41 matches.

Lino was then integrated into Diego Simeone’s Atletico side and made 65 La Liga appearances across two seasons, but he opted to return to Brazil in January 2025, joining Flamengo for a then club-record €22m (£18.4m) and signing a four-year contract.

With several big European clubs said to be interested in Lino, the winger may be tempted by a return to Europe heading into the prime years of his career.

Meanwhile, Everton are reportedly ready to battle fellow Premier League side Nottingham Forest for a £12.5m-rated centre-back from Brazil.

#1921. Celtic succession plan slammed as Dermot Desmond tipped to avoid December ‘chaos’ with digital move

Celtic’s board have been slammed for their lack of ambition and told it feels like they have “no plan” for when Martin O’Neill finally exits his role as manager.

Main shareholder Dermot Desmond and the board have faced several protests over the last 12 months, with the hierarchy at loggerheads with Celtic support over how the club is run, their perceived lack of footballing ambition and player recruitment.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recently, ultras fan group The Green Brigade has announced a boycott of all Scottish Cup matches and home Europa League fixtures, and former Celtic winger Charlie Nicholas admits he is concerned for the Scottish champions’ future, with tensions building ahead of the club’s annual AGM next month.

“Dermot Desmond is doing everything he can to frustrate the hardcore fans by not spending any money,” said Nicholas, speaking on the No Tippy Tappy Football Podcast from Footy Accumulators and BOYLE Sports. “They’re in turmoil with supporters, and that’s not going to go away. There’s an AGM coming up on 1 December, which was chaotic last season. They had to abandon it, and I don’t know how they’re going to get around this.

“There’s talk it might go digital rather than in person. But they’ve got major overheads, and Martin and his staff are finding it difficult to overcome this, because a lot of supporters aren’t going. Our judgement of Celtic is always going to be about Europe. We’ve won one game, and we only just got through it at the tail end of the other week. It’s not been good. The standard at the moment is very disappointing, to say the least.”

Nicholas, who won every domestic honour with Celtic during two spells in his playing career, is also concerned about how the club will replace veteran manager O’Neill when he decides his time in the game is over. The 74-year-old signed a one-year contract with the option of a further year in the summer. However, Nicholas isn’t convinced the club has a plan in place for when the Irishman boss calls time on his management.

Former Celtic loanee Robbie Keane was strongly linked to the vacant role in the summer, but talks were shelved after backlash from fans who were angered by the 46-year-old’s decision to remain in charge of Israeli side Maccabi Tel Aviv during the outbreak of the nation’s war against Gaza in 2023, with a section of Celtic fans openly supporting Palestine in the conflict.

“There have been a few suggested replacements for Martin O’Neill,” said Nicholas. “The strong talk in the summer was that they went after Robbie Keane. The word was that he more or less had the job, and that he’s still sitting in the background. That leads me into the debate that will continue with some sections of the Celtic fans and the shareholders. Until they get round that, there doesn’t look to be any evidence of a plan.

“What’s the next step of the ladder? Are we ready for Martin when he leaves? No, I don’t think they are ready. I just don’t know if the major shareholder is really wholehearted about it. There’s no one at the football club taking that responsibility now, so we’re drifting along at the moment. That’s why I understand where the real Celtic fans’ frustration is.”

For those who are unfamiliar with the new hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE company.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. “With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

In terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

From there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime shows.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment company, he leaves behind a role with Big 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

Given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the company take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as big as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.

#1919. Scotland best and worst case Euro 2028 qualifying draw scenarios as seeding pots confirmed

Scotland's potential qualification opponents for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - have been finalised following the conclusion of the Nations League group stage.

Seeding pots for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place in Belfast on Sunday, December 6, were based solely on the performance of each team in the Nations League across the 2026 campaign.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sebastien Pocognoli's men have been placed in Pot 3 due to finishing third in Group B1 after taking seven points from a possible 18 in an underwhelming start to life under the Belgian head coach.

Scotland finished nine points behind group winners Switzerland, who put seven goals past them without reply over two matches, and four points behind runners-up Slovenia, who also won at Hampden after a goalless draw in Ljubjlana. North Macedonia, who Scotland defeated home and away, finished bottom of the group on zero points.

Attention now turns to the Euro 2028 qualifiers, which will feature six groups of four and six groups of five. The five-team groups will begin their qualification campaign in March 2027 while the groups of four will not start until September 2027.

If Scotland are drawn into a group of four they will face a 10-month wait for their next competitive fixture with friendlies required to fill the empty calendar for March and June next year.

However, Scotland are more likely to be drawn into a group of five due to Uefa tilting the odds in favour of teams who are not involved in any Nations League play-offs or quarter-finals in March.

This would see Scotland play eight qualifiers instead of six, kicking off in March with further games in June, September/October and November.

Scotland cannot be drawn in a group with their co-hosts England, Wales or Republic of Ireland. While Northern Ireland are no longer staging tournament matches after Casement Park was dropped from the bid, they retain a special status in the qualifying draw and will also be kept apart from the co-hosts.

Scotland will draw one team each from Pots 1, 2, and 4, plus one team from Pot 5 if placed into one of the six five-team groups.

Here are the confirmed seeding pots and possible opponents for Scotland:

Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain. (England excluded).

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey. (Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland, Wales excluded).

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

Pot 5: Andorra, Azerbaijan, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Malta.

A dream draw for Scotland would involve facing the lowest ranked nations from each pot. Such a group would involve Greece, Bosnia & Herzegovina, San Marino and Gibraltar.

Another more favourable draw would pair Scotland with Denmark, Czechia, Moldova and Liechtenstein.

The nightmare scenario for Scotland would be drawing the highest ranked nation from each pot, which would involve matches against Spain, Switzerland, Finland and Azerbaijan.

Another more difficult draw would involve Scotland facing France, Austria, Bulgaria and Lithuania.

To qualify automatically for Euro 2028 Scotland must finish as one of the 12 group winners or eight best runners-up. The other four group runners-up enter the play-offs.

There is, however, a potential safety net for Scotland with Uefa reserving two spots for co-hosts who do not achieve qualification on the pitch. Assuming England as pot one seeds qualify, Scotland will be competing with Wales and Republic of Ireland to get in through the back door.

If two co-hosts qualify on the pitch, then Scotland and the other co-host who fail to qualify would automatically take advantage of the safety net.

The only scenario where Scotland would fail to make it to Euro 2028 via the safety net is if three co-hosts fail to qualify and Scotland's qualification record is the worst of the trio.

Scotland are only guaranteed to play Euro 2028 matches at Hampden if they qualify the proper way. Using the safety net opens the door to potentially playing their matches elsewhere.

Scotland have been branded “boring” under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli and urged to rip up their current game plan to get back on track.

Pocognoli, 39, has won just two of his first six games in charge of the national team, and came in for some scathing criticism in the wake of the 4-0 Nations League defeat to Switzerland on Monday night, with many supporters believing the manager is struggling to adapt his tactics to fit the strengths of the squad.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Former Scotland international Don Hutchison believes Pocognoli’s side have looked predictable under their new manager, and believes the squad must take inspiration from fellow home nation Northern Ireland, who achieved promotion to League A of the Nations League with a battling 1-1 draw away to Hungary on Tuesday night.

“Watching Scotland last night I was bored,” he wrote on his official X account. “Watching the same football I see a hundred times over. Northern Ireland are a good example of not over playing for the sake of it. Why can’t Scotland use a fighting, energy, ratting with “intensity”? Forget this ‘keep ball style’ - it doesn’t suit Scotland.”

Hutchison, who earned 26 caps for Scotland and is best remembered for scored the winning goal in a 1-0 European Championship playoff second-leg victory over England at Wembley in November 1999, thinks that the current national team are a shining example of what can be achieved when a team plays with more intensity.

“Yep that’s how you do it,” he said after Northern Ireland’s draw with Hungary in Budapest. “Bottle. Character. Heart. Fitness and desire. Well organised but with a willingness to run hard. Well played Northern Ireland. “[Scotland should] Try something different. Why do Scotland think they can ‘out football’ the opposition? We haven’t got enough players to make that work. Just go a bit longer and get the fans engaged in the game. [Scotland were playing] tippy tappy football last night.”

Despite some stinging criticism, Pocognoli defended his side’s performance in St Gallen, saying it had some of the “best moments” he’s seen from his team so far in his half-dozen games in charge. Speaking to the BBC, he said: “The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game, if I'm really honest and objective. We had some very good moments in the game, we started the game like we wanted, aggressive away from home. We could decide to be low on the pitch, but we did what we wanted to plan.

“We played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments in the game, and we faced Switzerland with different shapes and adapted well from the first minute. We conceded the goal from maybe one of the first chances they had. We also created chances, but we missed it. It means we were not clinical in that moment in the box.”

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 18:25, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 18:28

Incoming Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has refused to be drawn on suggestions that the club could target USA players in the upcoming transfer windows.

Pochettino is leaving his role with the USA in order to take charge of Man United.

The Argentine is expected to arrive in England on Wednesday morning after managing the United States in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti.

Since being appointed head coach of the 20-time English champions, there have been suggestions that Man United could look to target players who are well-known to Pochettino from his time in charge of the national side.

Juventus' Weston McKennie, Villarreal's Alex Freeman, Bournemouth's Tyler Adams and Monaco's Folarin Balogun are among those to be linked with switches.

"Now is not the time [to talk about this]. All the good players always have dreams to reach the highest level. And I think Man United is one of the teams that is in the highest level and it's the dream for many of the players," Pochettino told reporters.

"But now, I think they need to be focused on today, on tomorrow's game, on their clubs. I know really well for more than two years every single player.

"And I think they are all players with unbelievable talent. Of course, in the future, when that happens, of course we are going to pay attention, you know, to make some decisions and to pay attention to players that we know really well."

McKennie, who has previously played in the Premier League for Leeds United, also discussed the possibility of some of the national team's players making the move to Man United.

"I think obviously his time here, I think he's obviously grown to like this team and seen the quality that this team has to offer," he said during a pre-match press conference.

"And yeah, I think it's a potential. I think we have a lot of guys on our team that are due to probably make moves soon or within the next year. And so I think it's kind of inevitable.

"But at the end of the day, you never know what's going on in a coach's mind and what players that he's actually looking for. But I think he could potentially see some of the guys from here being talked about to go to Man U and potentially it happening."

Pochettino has a record of 22 wins, two draws and 12 defeats from his 36 matches in charge of the United States.

#1916. When is the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, who could Scotland play and when does qualifying begin

Scotland will soon discover which opponents they will face as they look to qualify for the third consecutive European Championship under new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.

Ending a 23-year exile from major tournaments by sealing a spot at Euro 2020 (played in 2021) under former manager Steve Clarke, they repeated the trick three years later, edging out Norway for a spot in the 2024 tournament in Germany.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Now under new boss Pocognoli, a disappointing third-placed finish in the Nations League has made Scotland’s hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028 - a tournament they will co-host - slightly harder after results meant they were placed in Pot 3 of the draw.

Want to know when the draw will take place, how to watch and which teams Scotland could face and which they will avoid? Here is everything you need to know about the Euro 2028 qualifying draw:

The qualifying draw for the European Championships in 2028 will take place in Belfast, Northern Ireland, on Sunday 6 December 2026. The tournament will be co-hosted by the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland.

If you want to stream the draw via your smart TV, laptop, tablet or mobile phone, the entire ceremony will be streamed for free via UEFA.tv and via the official UEFA YouTube channel.

Scotland’s third-placed finish in Nations League Group B1 means they will be placed into Pot 3 of the draw next month. They will be drawn against once team each from Pots 1, 2 and 4 and potentially pot 5, depending on if they are placed into one of the six five-team groups.

They can’t be drawn against England, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland or Wales, with UEFA keeping the tournament co-hosts separated in the qualifying phase of Euro 2028.

Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain.

Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkiye.

Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland, Slovakia, Ukraine.

Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino.

The Euro 2028 qualifiers begin in March 2027, but Scotland’s campaign will depend entirely on the outcome of the qualifying draw in December.

As attested to above, Scotland will be placed into either a four-team or five-team group. If they are drawn in a four team group, fixtures will begin in March 2027. However, should they be drawn in a five team group, their first Euro 2028 qualifying fixture will take place in September 2027.

#1914. Jurgen Klopp loves him but Brajan Gruda may never play for Brighton again

Brajan Gruda arrived at Brighton in 2024 as one of Europe's hottest prospects.

Albion paid around £25m to Mainz for the German playmaker as he joined on a four-year contract.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"I saw the big impact he made in the Bundesliga and he's a player I admire a lot," said Brighton’s German head coach Fabian Hurzeler at the time.

Hurzeler also admired Gruda's style of play and describe the then 20-year-old as a "street footballer."

Jurgen Klopp used the same "street baller" term this week as Gruda - now 22 - made an impressive start to his senior Germany career.

He netted a fine individual goal on his full debut against Serbia last week and then grabbed a goal and two assists as Germany walloped the Netherlands 5-0 last night. Brighton's Bart Verbruggen was in goal for the Dutch.

After Gruda's excellent debut against Serbia, Klopp said he felt sorry for their left back Petar Sukacev. "That left-back, he's a poor lad!" said the former Liverpool boss Klopp.

Opta statistics backed up Klopp’s claim as they stated nine of Gruda's 14 dribbles against Serbia were successful.

"He's a fantastic player who loves to take people on and hasn't yet fulfilled his potential. He doesn't need to at his age, but he's shown an awful lot of positive signs," Klopp said.

So will he play for Brighton again and why did the Seagulls loan him out? Gruda made 45 appearances for Albion under Hurzeler in all competitions and showed glimpses of his potential with four goals and eight assists.

Niggling injuries and the fitness demands of the Premier League saw Gruda struggle to make a sustained impact. At times he featured in the No 10 role but largely he was behind the powerful Yankuba Minteh for the right wing slot.

Minteh joined for £30m in the same window as Gruda but the Gambian adapted faster. Gruda made just eight Premier League starts in the 2025-26 season and a change of environment was deemed beneficial by all parties and he joined RB Leipzig on loan for the second half of last campaign

“Brajan wants regular football, and we are not able to guarantee him that in the second half of the season," said Hurzeler.

Three goals and three assists for Leipzig in the Bundesliga convinced them to extend the loan for another season and Brighton were happy to sanction another temporary deal.

Sporting director Mike Cave said, “Brajan had a good second half of the season with Leipzig and was keen to explore the opportunity of remaining there for the coming year.

“This is a move that allows Brajan to continue to secure regular playing time at a good level, in an environment he knows well.”

Brighton are pretty sharp on their loan agreements but no doubt they will now be double checking the small print of the loan contract.

Leipzig are believed to have an obligation to buy at the end of the season, albeit with certain conditions - but the size of any potential transfer fee remains unclear.

His value is clearly going upwards and the loan agreement will likely allow Brighton to cash in, should they decide to sell. Further high-profile displays for Klopp's Germany will see that increase.

Gruda remains contracted with Albion until 2028 and this week Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen were also credited with interest.

Transfer expert Florian Plettenberg posted: “The obligation to buy for Brajan Gruda will be activated in 2027 due to accounting reasons. The total package for RB Leipzig will amount to €30m, including bonuses. Gruda will then get a contract until 2031, which has already been agreed.

“Bayern have always had him on their list, even before his move to Brighton. However, he is currently not a concrete transfer target for Bayern – unless something extraordinary happens, such as the sale of Michael Olise.”

Gruda seems to prefer living and playing his football in Germany and whether he even considers moving back to Brighton remains to be seen. The Seagulls - who are flying high in the Premier League - also have a number of options on the right flank.

Minteh - who almost joined Liverpool last summer - is just returning from injury, while Paraguayan international Diego Gomez has also excelled in the wide right position this term.

Zadok Yohanna, Femi Azeez, Malick Yalcouye are all available, while the likes of Amario Cozier-Duberry and Harry Howell are out on loan.

Gruda's form is impressive but whether he returns to the Premier League with Brighton anytime soon is debatable. Attention will now likely turn to maximising their fee.

France star Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after being hit with a nasty elbow in France's 3-1 defeat to Italy in the Nations League.

The PSG winger was left in need of some emergency dental work by Italy's Davide Frattesi who caught the 21-year-old in the mouth while shielding the ball.

In his post match interview French boss Zinedine Zidane, when asked if Doue had lost a tooth, replied: 'Yeah I think so. We’re going to take him straight there, a tooth has come loose I think, we’ll take care of him starting tomorrow.'

It was a poor day all round for the Frenchman who not only had his tooth dislodged but was also unable to impact a poor game for Les Blues in which the Azzuri beat them at the San Siro.

To compound Doue's misery it was the offender Frattesi who scored Italy's second goal in the 3-1 win just six minutes before he performed some unorthodox dentistry.

The Lazio midfielder's goal completed the Italians' comeback after going 1-0 down to a Michael Olise goal just ten minutes in before Inter Milan's Francesco Esposito levelled things up just 16 minutes later.

Desire Doue was left with a loose front tooth after receiving an elbow in the mouth from Davide Fratessi

Fratessi got away with just a yellow card as Italy beat the French 3-1 at the San Siro

Frattesi gave Italy the lead early on in the second half before Esposito netted his second from the spot to put the game out of reach.

Speaking after the game Zidane was surprisingly positive about his team's performance despite the loss, saying that losing is, 'part of the process.'

The French then went onto say: 'The most important thing is creating chances. Hitting the post had an impact, but I'm not disappointed.

'I would have been if we hadn't created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren't at the right level off the ball.'

The World Cup winner was not entirely positive however, later saying: 'in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively.'

The victory put Italy level on points with the French in Group A with both sides having won three drawn one and lost one.

But France will have an opportunity to right their wrongs and return to the top of the group on Sunday as they welcome Turkey.

But if Italy beat Belgium on the same day the French will have to settle for second.

#1910. Germany vs. Netherlands lineups confirmed: Jurgen Klopp, Xavi decisions made for Nations League decider

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 18:39, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 19:08

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has made two changes to his starting lineup for this evening’s UEFA Nations League decider against the Netherlands at the Olympiastadion in Berlin.

Both changes come in defence, with centre-back Nico Schlotterbeck and left-back Nathaniel Brown coming in to replace Malick Thiaw and Maximilian Mittelstadt respectively.

Schlotterbeck and Brown are joined in a four-man backline by Philipp Treu and Jonathan Tah, protecting Ajax goalkeeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

Captain Joshua Kimmich will earn his 118th international cap alongside Bayern Munich teammate Aleksandar Pavlovic, with Liverpool playmaker Florian Wirtz operating in the number 10 role.

Brajan Gruda, who along with Wirtz scored in Germany's 3-1 win against Serbia last Friday, retains his starting spot in attack along with Derry Scherhant and centre-forward Kai Havertz.

Germany know that they will climb from third to first position in League A Group B if they beat the Netherlands and Greece fail to beat Serbia, while Klopp's men can secure at least a quarter-final place if they draw in Berlin and Greece lose.

As for the Netherlands, head coach Xavi has made just the one change to the side that began the 7-0 thrashing of Greece in Amsterdam last Friday.

Crystal Palace midfielder Quinten Timber has been recalled at the expense of injured Barcelona star Frenkie de Jong who sustained a back problem against Greece.

This means that Timber and his brother Jurrien Timber of Arsenal – who netted a brace against Greece – will start together for just the second time on the international stage, having previously done so against Greece in October.

In the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Denzel Dumfries will captain the Oranje at right-back, joining Jan Paul van Hecke, Micky Van de Ven and Jurrien Timber in a four-man defence playing in front of goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Quinten Timber will link up with Joey Veerman and Tijjani Reijnders in a three-man midfield, the latter of whom netted a 33-minute first-half hat-trick against Greece.

In-form Roma striker Donyell Malen was also on the scoresheet last time out and will continue to lead the line next to fellow attackers Crysencio Summerville and Cody Gakpo, who scored a 92nd-minute equaliser in the 1-1 draw with Germany in September.

Netherlands head into this contest knowing they will finish top of their group and qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals if they avoid defeat against Germany, while they can also qualify if Greece fail to beat Serbia.

Germany starting lineup: Ter Stegen; Treu, Tah, Schlotterbeck, Brown; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Gruda, Wirtz, Scherhant; Havertz

Subs: Urbig, Nubel, Thiaw, Baku, Nmecha, Füllkrug, Bischof, Jeltsch, Mittelstadt, El Mala, Karl, Ebnoutalib

Netherlands starting lineup: Verbruggen; Dumfries, Van de Ven; Van Hecke, J. Timber; Q. Timber, Veerman, Reijnders; Summerville, Malen, Gakpo

Subs: Roefs, Flekken, Geertruida, Maatsen, Van den Berg, Kluivert, Meerdink, Til, Lang, Van Bommel, Koopmeiners, Zechiel

#1907. Declan Rice says England ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain

Declan Rice says the England squad ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain in their final Nations League group game.

England earned top spot in their Nations League group and ended Spain’s extraordinary 43-game unbeaten run with a thrilling 3-2 win in Madrid.

Thomas Tuchel’s side scored three goals in 12 minutes either side of half-time to stun Spain before withstanding a late siege to seal their finest win under the German boss.

Harry Kane took his international tally to 93 goals with a penalty on the stroke of half-time as England deservedly ended the opening 45 minutes ahead.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White then scored twice in the space of four minutes to open up a commanding 3-0 lead over the shell-shocked Spaniards.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Elliot Anderson’s red card on 63 minutes and Mikel Oyarzabal’s subsequent penalty offered Spain a route back into a match they looked out of.

England fans feared a collapse similar to the one the team suffered in last summer’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second with 20 minutes remaining.

But this time England kept their opponents at bay with some resolute defending and two superb saves from goalkeeper James Trafford.

Rice was full of praise for his teammates after the Nations League win and said he ‘knew’ England would beat the world champions in their own backyard.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ Rice told ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

"We knew we were going to beat them tonight!"Declan Rice after England's win over Spain in Madrid 🇪🇸🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/dbNiMi74od

‘Our first ten minutes were probably the best we’ve played. It was pressure, pressure, pressure – we could have had two or three.

‘If we don’t go down to ten men, we see more of the ball, we start to see them jump more, we start to see more space, and we start to see our attacking players thrive like they were doing in the second half.

‘With ten men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against that team is massive. It’s a massive win. Credit to everyone.

‘When they got the second, you might have thought that it was going to go the other way with the amount of pressure they were putting on, but that resilience.

‘Keep emptying the tank, doing anything for this badge, for this team, for our players, for the manager.’

Meanwhile, Tuchel hailed England’s ‘brilliant performance’ after they beat a side who last lost in regulation play in March 2024.

‘Brilliant performance. Well deserved win,’ he said. ‘Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

‘It was a long 30 minutes after the red card but I don’t want to focus on that. There were so many positive things in the first 60 minutes.

‘Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level.

‘We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.’

#1905. Luis de la Fuente singles out ‘fantastic’ England star after Spain defeat

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente said when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the important tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’

#1904. Coritiba vs Santos - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 16 Nov 2026 20:01, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 10:52

Coritiba will be looking to move closer to securing their Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A status when they welcome Santos to the Estadio Major Antonio Couto Pereira on Wednesday.

The hosts sit 13th in the table with 42 points from 34 matches, five clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors occupy ninth place on 47 points and are hoping to strengthen their push for a place in next season's Copa Libertadores.

Coritiba head into Wednesday's encounter having lost 1-0 away to Internacional in their last league outing, with the defeat preventing them from recording consecutive victories after previously beating Vitoria 2-0 at home.

The result in Porto Alegre extended a difficult period for the Coxa, who have now recorded just one win in their last nine league matches, losing six times and drawing twice during that run.

Coritiba will be keen to make the most of home advantage and take another step towards the 45-point target they have identified for securing top-flight survival, particularly after winning their most recent home fixture.

Guilherme Bossle is expected to remain in interim charge following Fernando Seabra's dismissal, having overseen the victory against Vitoria before the narrow defeat to Internacional, and his immediate priority will be to improve the team's consistency with only three league fixtures remaining after Wednesday's match.

Santos, meanwhile, arrive in Curitiba looking to end a three-match winless run in the league, having drawn with Bahia and Palmeiras before suffering a 2-1 defeat away to Red Bull Bragantino.

The Peixe had briefly improved their position with a 2-1 victory over Fluminense, but they have since struggled to turn promising performances into wins, recording just one victory in their last six league matches (D3, L2), leaving them six points behind sixth-placed Bahia and with ground to make up in the race for continental qualification.

Cuca's side have nevertheless been more productive in front of goal, scoring 50 times in the league, with only five teams finding the net more frequently.

The head-to-head record is another reason for Santos to approach the fixture with confidence, as they have lost only once in the last 10 meetings between the clubs, winning seven and drawing two.

However, Santos were beaten by Coritiba earlier this season, suffering a 3-0 defeat on home soil, although the recent trend in this fixture favours the visitors, with the away team winning three of the last four competitive meetings.

The clubs have also met three times in 2026, including their Copa do Brasil tie, in which Santos progressed after winning 2-0 in Curitiba following a draw in the first leg.

Coritiba will be without goalkeeper Pedro Morisco, who is away with the Brazil national team and is not expected to return to Curitiba in time for Wednesday's fixture, meaning Pedro Rangel is set to start between the posts.

Defender Jacy is also a doubt after suffering a knee problem against Internacional, with the centre-back still undergoing treatment and yet to return to full training, while Lucas Ronier remains unavailable after suffering a serious knee injury.

Santos will welcome back Willian Arao and Gonzalo Escobar, who have recovered from thigh injuries and returned to unrestricted training with the first team.

Thaciano has also resumed working with the squad, although Gabriel Brazao and Lucas Veríssimo remain sidelined, while Alvaro Barreal and Vinicius Lira are also unavailable.

Gabriel Bontempo, Miguelito and Gustavo Caballero have been away on international duty, leaving Cuca with some decisions to make when selecting his squad.

Neymar is available again after having his suspension reduced, while Gabriel Barbosa is expected to lead the attack after scoring 15 goals in the 2026 Campeonato Brasileiro.

Rangel; Tinga, Tiago Coser, Moledo, B. Melo; Gomez, Santos; Lavega, Josue, Lopes; Rocha

Diogenes; Rodinei, Arao, Peres, Escobar; Henrique, Oliva; Coutinho, Neymar, Everton; Barbosa

Coritiba have the advantage of playing at home and will be encouraged by their victory over Santos earlier in the season, but their recent results have been inconsistent.

The visitors have also struggled to win recently, although they still possess enough attacking quality to find the net, making a draw a reasonable outcome.

#1902. Thomas Tuchel speaks out on James Trafford vs Jordan Pickford battle for England spot

Thomas Tuchel insists that England do not have a number one, after James Trafford made a brilliant case to be first choice goalkeeper in the win over Spain.

Trafford played the full game as the Three Lions pulled off a memorable 3-2 Nations League win over the world champions in Madrid.

It was a stunning first hour from Tuchel’s side and the visitors were 3-0 up on 57 minutes thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Things started to unravel a bit from there as Elliot Anderson was shown a straight red card and Mikel Oyarzabal converted from the penalty spot.

Nico Williams then made it a very nervy climax for England as he scored on 75 minutes and the hosts pushed for an equaliser.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Trafford helped his team stand firm, though, including making a tremendous double save late on.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has been first choice goalkeeper since 2018, winning 94 caps, but his place is now in doubt thanks to the emergence of Trafford.

James Trafford last-gasp double save 🤯🤯#UNLSaves | @Betano_PT pic.twitter.com/K3Rn995OEE

Tuchel was not ready to declare either stopper his number one, but was clearly very impressed by the Leeds United star.

‘There’s no number one,’ said the England boss. ‘It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted. He had a brilliant match. It only works if you’re top from number one to 11.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Tuchel continued on Trafford: ‘Very good. That’s his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.

‘The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.’

The German has also liked what he has seen from Trafford on the ball, saying: ‘There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

‘Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half.

‘With everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.’

At 24 years old, Trafford is eight years younger than Pickford and looks to be his successor, even if he has not entirely displaced him just yet.

The win in Spain meant England topped their Nations League group and will play a runner-up from another group in the quarter-finals of the competition.

Groups A2 and A4 come to an end on Monday and Tuesday respectively, which is when we will learn England’s possible opponents for Friday’s draw.

Belgium have already secured second place in group A1, so they are a possible opponent for the Three Lions in the quarter-finals that are played in March next year.

Former Leeds United man Danny Mills believes 'exceptional' Brighton can achieve Champions League football this season.

The Seagulls have emerged as surprise title contenders this term and are currently second, five points adrift of leaders Arsenals.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton are the leading scorers in the division with 26 goals from 10 matches. They have also been impressive at the back with seven clean sheets from 10 matches.

Mills, speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer the latest football odds, said: "Brighton would need a little bit of luck, possibly with injuries. We've seen Leicester do it in the past.

"Are they likely to win it? Probably not. But is Europa League or Champions League football a possibility with the league the way it is in flux at the moment. Absolutely.

"[Brighton] are incredibly well coached. If you listen to some of the best players that I've ever been around, the likes of Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, that have seen these up first hand and seen some of the coaching that Fabian Hurzeler is doing, it's exceptional.

"It's clear, it's concise, they have a specific plan that they work to, and it's working for them. I think they will keep it up but they will be tested at some point.

"Undoubtedly there will be a dip at some point within that. But at the moment they're playing with great confidence in what they're doing, great confidence and belief in their manager."

Mills was also full of praise for Brighton transfer model and the fact they give new players and youngsters a chance to shine on the biggest stage.

"I think we've seen in recent years the business model has changed somewhat. I think you have to look at it, you know, teams understand now that bringing in young players and making them better, EPPP ripped the heart out of the academy system, really.

“So all the top clubs took all the best young players very, very early and clubs were not getting huge fees for them at that stage. So I think what they're trying to do now is hold on to these players a little bit longer, develop these players, give themselves a chance.

“I think we've seen it across the leagues, that's the model. It's going back to maybe the old days of let's give players an opportunity, let's give them plenty of game time, improve them, and then sell them on and keep doing the same thing.

“It's no different from the Brentford model, the Brighton model. It's exactly what they're doing. So then identification and recruitment in all that is absolutely key.”

#1900. Man Utd told Chelsea star would be ‘good signing’ for Mauricio Pochettino

Mikael Silvestre has encouraged Manchester United to explore a move for Estevao – but doubts the forward could be coaxed to the Theatre of Dreams as he appears intent on ‘fighting for his place’ at Chelsea.

United spent in the region of £160million on new signings in the summer, with club chiefs showing they were prepared to back Michael Carrick following an impressive third-place finish.

But any optimism that had grown amongst the fanbase in the back-end of last season rapidly faded as a 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea last month extended the Red Devils’ miserable winless run to nine matches in all competitions.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Naturally, attentions have quickly turned towards the January transfer window, when United will be expected to splash the cash in the hope of boosting their prospects for the second half of the campaign.

United chiefs are set to resurrect their pursuit of a left-back as a priority to provide support for Luke Shaw after missing out on Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

According to Silvestre, Chelsea winger Estevao could represent a ‘good signing’ for United, with the Brazilian having made just one start in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That start happened to come against United, though, and the 19-year-old was widely praised for his performance as goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer proved decisive at Stamford Bridge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Well, Estevao played against United for Chelsea, and I think he’s shown why he should feature more,’ Silvestre told Betarades.gr.

‘It looks like he’s going to fight for his place in the team, so I don’t anticipate United making a move for him.

‘But he’s a good player for sure. He’s playing for the national team of Brazil, and I like his style. If he were available, he would be a good signing for United.’

Asked why Newcastle and England star Hall may ‘make sense’ for United at left-back, Silvestre replied: ‘Lewis Hall had an impressive season with Newcastle, and he’s been on the club’s radar for sure.

‘The club made an attempt to sign him and other fullbacks, but couldn’t get it done.

‘They now have to rely on Luke Shaw, Diego Dalot, on Noussair Mazraoui, and on Patrick Dorgu, who has also been injured for quite some time. So that’s not been helpful either.’

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

#1898. Corinthians vs Botafogo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 16 Nov 2026 22:02

Relegation-threatened Corinthians will be looking to climb out of the Brasileirao drop zone when they welcome Copa Sudamericana hopefuls Botafogo to the Neo Quimica Arena this midweek..

The hosts sit 17th in the Brazilian top-flight table after 34 matches, one point behind 16th-placed Internacional, while the visitors are 12th and above 13th-placed Coritiba by virtue of goal difference.

Corinthians ended a 10-match winless league run with victory over Mirassol on matchday 33, and although they failed to secure back-to-back wins following their goalless draw at Sao Paulo last time out, taking a point from that encounter was still an impressive result for a side that had lost each of their previous five league away matches.

The result also means that the Timao have kept consecutive clean sheets after conceding in each of their previous 10 matches during that winless Brasileiro spell, reflecting the improvement in resilience since Clarence Seedorf took over the reins in October.

Fernando Diniz was sacked after the club suffered seven consecutive league defeats, before interim boss William Batista also lost to Palmeiras, but Corinthians have since recorded three results without defeat in four matches under Seedorf's guidance, with the only blemish being a 3-2 setback against Vasco da Gama on October 24.

Knowing that victory this midweek would lift his side temporarily out of the relegation zone, pending Internacional's game against Vasco later on, the former AC Milan midfielder will look to build on the fact that the Timao ended a five-match winless home league run with their victory over Mirassol.

Corinthians have now taken 22 points from their 17 matches at the Neo Quimica Arena in the top-flight campaign, a return that leaves the Sao Paulo-based team with the third-worst home record in the division.

Botafogo, meanwhile, head into this encounter looking to build on their 1-0 victory over Atletico-MG last time out, with Edenilson's 19th-minute goal proving decisive and lifting the Fire into the Copa Sudamericana zone.

The result also ended a two-match losing streak following defeats to Internacional and Remo, while marking Tite's second victory in seven games since his appointment in September and making him the club's third permanent manager of the season after the dismissals of Martin Anselmi and Franclim Carvalho.

Botafogo have now recorded 11 victories from their 34 league matches (D9, L14) this term, scoring 46 goals and conceding 53, meaning there is still room for improvement at both ends of the pitch.

Another victory could lift the Fire as high as 10th, depending on the results of 11th-placed Vasco and 10th-placed Sao Paulo, who both play on Thursday, although Wednesday's visitors are winless in each of their last six away games (D1, L5).

However, Botafogo can draw inspiration from the fact that they are unbeaten in their last five meetings with Corinthians and have recorded victories in three of those outings, including a 3-1 success in the most recent meeting between the two sides.

Corinthians will be without Yuri Alberto, Matheus Pereira and Andre Ramalho, with the first two suspended following their red cards last time out, while the latter is unavailable due to an accumulation of bookings.

Zakaria Labyad and Kayke remain long-term absentees with anterior cruciate ligament injuries, while Rodrigo Garro, Alex Santana, Raniele and former Arsenal defender Gabriel Paulista are working towards full fitness and remain doubtful.

André Luiz will also be unavailable for Corinthians after the CBF rejected the club's request to release him early from Brazil duty, with the midfielder set to remain with the national team for their friendly against Singapore on November 17, just a day before the clash with Botafogo.

Botafogo are expected to be without Nahuel Ferraresi, whose return from international duty could come too late for any major involvement, while Jordan Barrera is ruled out of the season with injury and Danilo is a doubt due to an adductor problem.

Arthur Chaves is still being assessed by the medical department, with Kaio Pantaleao also being targeted for a return after working towards full fitness.

H Souza; Matheuzinho, J Pedro, G Henrique, Angileri; Carrillo, Bidon; Kaio Cesar, Vitinho, Bidu; Depay

Batista; Vitinho, Justino, Marçal, Telles; C Medina, Edenilson; Ziyech, Montoro,  Martins; Soares

Corinthians have the greater need for points and should be motivated by the opportunity to move closer to safety, but their poor home record makes it difficult to back them to claim all three.

Botafogo have been inconsistent in recent weeks, yet their stronger league position and unbeaten run against the hosts suggest that Tite's side can leave Sao Paulo with a share of the points.

#1897. Newhaven halt Robins’ flight towards play-off place

The Dockers flew out of the traps and would have been ahead with barely a minute on the clock were it not for a great save from the Hassocks keeper to keep out a Matt Gunn header.

Within a minute, Gunn had gone close with another header, before a brilliant Harry Reed cross narrowly evaded the onrushing Tyler Capon.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Thomas Sekyere then went close before Hassocks mustered their first attempt on target; young keeper Jake Rhodes, making his senior debut in Pike’s absence, pulling off a great save from close-range to keep the score goalless.

Newhaven soon resumed control of proceedings, with Matt Feeney-Hill drawing a save from the keeper, before Lee Robinson headed a pin-point Sekyere cross wide of the post.

Despite the game being open and flowing, it took until just after the hour mark for the first goal to arrive.

With 63 minutes on the clock, a Sekyere ball over the top set Robinson away, and he produced a sublime rasping finish from a tight angle to fire the hosts into a deserved lead.

Seven minutes later, it was two as Robinson notched his second. Hassocks failed to fully clear a set-piece, Ross Barclay hooked the ball back into the danger zone, Gunn won a header, and Robinson produced a fine finish on the turn to double the Docker’s advantage.

There was to be no coast to the finish line for Newhaven, though, with the Robins roaring back into the game in the last 20 minutes.

Harvey Blake was inches away from pulling a goal back, with his well-struck effort cannoning off the upright, before Lewis Finney found space in a crowded penalty area to curl the ball beyond the grasp of Rhodes with 13 minutes of normal time left.

Aside from a Robinson effort that was smothered away by the Hassocks custodian, the final stages were largely played out in Newhaven’s defensive half.

With two minutes left of normal time remaining, the visitors seemed almost certain to complete their comeback when a loose ball fell kindly to Finney just inside the six-yard box, only for him to be denied by another superb close-range save by Rhodes.

However, the Dockers managed to cling onto what were a hard-fought but fully-deserved and mightily impressive three-points.

They now look to build on that victory this weekend when Lancing, themselves boosted by a 5-0 win at the weekend, visit Fort Road.

Di Paola told us: “It was a good game. I thought we played well. I thought we were dominant for 75 minutes of the game and then they came at us. They kept bringing on good players to try to get back into the game.
