#1892. Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 02:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:49 EST, 13 November 2026

England will head to Spain on Sunday for a Nations League shoot out with the World Champions. A win in Madrid could see Thomas Tuchel's team progress to the quarter-finals next March as group winners.

It wasn't always easy on Harry Kane's big night at Wembley against Croatia, though. Indeed this was probably England's worst performance since losing to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final last July.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the key issues emerging from last night's tight squeeze.

Self-defeating abuse of White is madness and must stop

In case nobody has noticed, England are not over stocked with competent right-backs.

Trent Alexander-Arnold isn't wholly trusted in big games by Thomas Tuchel, Reece James is always injured and Tino Livramento has also struggled to be available. Why, then, is a significant section of the England support so determined to drive Ben White away from the international scene?

White plays for Arsenal, the champions of England. He is a fine, versatile defender who would be gratefully received and appreciated by fans of most national teams in world football. He had issues with the previous England management regime and does not apologise for that.

Ben White was booed when he came on. The abuse towards the defender must stop

He spoke about it this week and made it clear he didn't wish to reopen old wounds. All that matters now is that he is willing and available. But – despite a plea from Tuchel before this game – England fans still booed him when he came on as a substitute last night.

It's a disgraceful way to treat a footballer who can be an asset to his country going forwards and it's something the England manager cares deeply about. Do we want to win the next Euros or not? Do we want our best players motivated and driven and part of the squad? Or do we want to faff about harbouring old grudges related to a situation in Qatar four winters ago that none of us really know that much about?

The choice is clear. If we are not careful, we will drive a good footballer away from the England set-up for good. It's madness.

Big night for Kane but questions for England

They came to celebrate Harry Kane and the England captain got his goal. Number 92 for the striker. Beneath all the fuss over England's talisman, however, this came perilously close to being a step backwards for Thomas Tuchel's England.

The England manager has been saying since the last international break in September and October that he wanted his team to go to Madrid on Sunday in with a shout at knocking Spain from the top of this Nations League Group. Had Croatia been a little smarter in front of goal at Wembley last night, England would have been heading for a dead rubber against the world champions.

Harry Kane scored on his big night as England edged out a 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley

It was a night to remember for Kane as he was honoured after receiving his record 126th cap

Three times in the last ten minutes of this game, Croatia had good opportunities to score a second goal and take a point from the game that would have been perfectly justified. So England crawled over the line but there was little here that was impressive with questions emerging once again about how capable really are when they don't have the ball.

Kane put it well himself afterwards when he said: 'You can't always expect things to be perfect. Of course, we know we can improve on a few bits and we will need to if we want to win on Sunday.'

Tuchel himself will perhaps have quiet concerns. One of the German's worries about this England team is that they sometimes struggle to take training performances on to the field and this was another case in point.

The ultimate target for this team is to win the home Euros in 2028 and the pressure will need handling in front of their own supporters if they are to do that. With that in mind, it's good to know that the FA are interested in hosting the finals of this Nations League competition next summer.

If England make it through next March's two-legged quarter-finals, they could do with some practice of playing high-stakes games at Wembley.

Asked last week on the day he announced his squad whether Jordan Pickford was still his number one goalkeeper, Tuchel was unequivocal.

'He is,' said Tuchel. 'But the competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And James Trafford will get regular starts now, that's what we wanted. They shared the matches last time. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again.'

Morgan Rogers impressed after opening the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour

Jordan Pickford starting against Croatia could lead to James Trafford playing against Spain

With all this in mind, it was expected that Trafford would start this game with Pickford getting the gloves for the one that really matters in Spain on Sunday. That wasn't the case, so we wait with interest to see what the England manager does in Madrid.

What nobody really wants is for a return to the situation we had in the 1980s when Ron Greenwood used to rotate between the late Ray Clemence and last night's guest of honour Peter Shilton.

England's back four is the one area of this team that can look unconvincing – they did again last night - and the last thing they need is not to know who their goalkeeper is from one match to the next. Tuchel is going to have to make a decision.

Interesting that Tuchel chose to put Dan Burn into his team for this game, despite the Newcastle defender not being in the original squad.

With Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa both absent with injuries, Everton's Jarrod Branthwaite would have expected to play on the left of Jarell Quansah here. Instead, Burn leapfrogged him in the queue and maybe we should have paid more attention to something Tuchel said the day before the game.

'Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,' said Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite clearly has a way to go before he's fully trusted to start by Thomas Tuchel

'You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe where they followed in a high press and to man-man. And of course he was with us at the World Cup so he is used a bit more to our style of play.'

That's all very well and logical but – that being the case – why was Branthwaite chosen ahead of Burn in the original group of 25 last Friday? Burn, as it happened, had a very good game last night.

Tuchel talks always about the value of players being in camp. 'The train is leaving the station,' is one of the England manager's more memorable quotes of recent times. Players like Cole Palmer, for example, have learned to their cost that missing meet-ups with injuries can be costly.

Bukayo Saka is not in that category and has plenty of credit in the bank with the England manager. However, Tuchel's fondness for Morgan Rogers is well known and Saka's absence does give him a way of getting the Chelsea player into his team. Rogers may be a number ten at heart but he was effective once again here out on the right side.

The 24-year-old was one of England's better players on a muted night against Croatia and he deserved his first half goal. He gives England a more direct, athletic dimension on the opposite flank to the more balletic offerings of Anthony Gordon. Food for thought for Tuchel at least as Saka continues his own battle against persistent injuries.

Bukayo Saka's long-term place in England's team could be under threat from Morgan Rogers

Newcastle United were pretty much an open door in the summer as they sold players left right and centre. Gordon to Barcelona to make sure the club was the right side of the financial guidelines and then Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal simply because the players made it known they wanted to go.

Strange, then, that Manchester United didn't make a proper move for left-back Lewis Hall. Admittedly this wasn't the most difficult match in which he will have ever played, but Hall was impressive once again.

With Luke Shaw so injury prone, Hall pretty much has the left-back berth sewn up for England but it feels as though he now needs to make the next step in his club career. United retain a nominal interest but who knows what incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino may think? It's hard to work out why United didn't try harder to sign him last summer. He has subsequently signed a new contract at Newcastle, of course.

Bexhill Amateur Athletic Club II secured a hard-fought 2-1 away victory over Robertsbridge United, with Dexter Bawn scoring both goals for the visitors. Danny Turner replied for Robertsbridge in the 85th minute, but Bexhill held firm to take the points.

There was no shortage of entertainment at St Leonards Social, where the hosts emerged victorious from an extraordinary ten-goal encounter against Herstmonceux. Social eventually ran out 6-4 winners, with Allan McMinigal and Rhys Brockhurst both scoring twice. Anotidaishe Tanaka and Matt Syrett were also on target as the home side claimed a memorable victory.

Parkfield produced one of the standout performances of the weekend, recording a remarkable 8-0 away victory over Sedlescombe Rangers. Jamie Salvidge and Jack Lugg both completed superb hat-tricks, while Neale Blackham and Bobby Bowles added a goal apiece to complete the rout. The result continued Parkfield's outstanding recent goalscoring form.

Northiam 75 also enjoyed a successful afternoon, defeating Battle Town II 3-1. Ricky Rogers, Brandon Smith and Tyler Wilson were the goalscorers for Northiam, while Alex Southall replied for the visitors. SC Pass & Move Arrows II secured a narrow 1-0 away victory over Ticehurst. The sides were level at half-time before Beni Isaac struck the decisive goal to earn Arrows all three points.

Division Three produced plenty of excitement, with Herstmonceux II edging an extraordinary nine-goal thriller against Hollington United III. The sides were remarkably level at 4-4 at half-time, but Herstmonceux found the only goal of the second period to secure a dramatic 5-4 away victory.

Eduart Zotaj scored twice for the visitors, with Max Attrell, Charlie Mackay and Fenton Webster also finding the net. For Hollington, Rhys Smith scored twice, while Marley Streeter and Michael Woodcock were also on target in a remarkable opening 45 minutes.

Hawkhurst United and Icklesham Casuals shared six goals in an entertaining 3-3 draw. Alfie Hillman scored twice for Icklesham, with Callum Hadaway also on target as the visitors returned home with a point.

Hollington Hawks secured a 4-2 home victory over Robertsbridge United II, thanks largely to an outstanding hat-trick from Chris Sanders. James Winchester added the fourth goal to complete a fine afternoon for the hosts.

Little Common III continued their positive run of results with a narrow 1-0 home victory over Northiam 75 II. Jay Abib scored the only goal of the game to secure another valuable three points for Common.

Bexhill Amateur Athletic Club produced an emphatic performance in the Sussex Intermediate Challenge Cup, defeating Westfield Reserves 6-0. Leo Oliver and Simon Walton both scored twice, while Jayden Douglin and Daniel Goergen also found the net as Bexhill comfortably secured their place in the next round.

There was plenty of excitement in the Hastings FA Junior Cup, where Ninfield II claimed an impressive 4-3 away victory over Mountfield United in a seven-goal thriller. The Junior Club Tackleway II also progressed, securing a 3-1 home victory over Catsfield.

#1890. Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham England Under-21 record

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has broken two England Under-21 records previously held by Jude Bellingham in a matter of days.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to play for the Three Lions at Under-21 level when he came off the bench on Friday in a 1-0 defeat to Portugal.

Dowman then started against France at Aston Gate on Monday night, scoring a dramatic late winner in a 3-2 victory.

His appearance against Portugal broke Bellingham’s record as youngest England Under-21 player and his goal against France broke the Real Madrid superstar’s record as youngest to score at this level.

Dowman was 16 years and 320 days when he scored in Bristol on Monday, while Bellingham was 17 years and 67 days old when he made his debut against Kosovo in 2020, scoring on his first appearance for England Under-21s.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Also on the scoresheet for England in the friendly win over France were Tottenham’s Mikey Moore and Manchester City’s Divin Mubama, who is on loan at Southampton this season.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis captained Lee Carsley’s side, while the likes of Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood and Liverpool’s Trey Nyoni were also in the starting XI.

It was Dowman who was making yet more history, though, having already become the youngest player to score in the Premier League and to make an appearance in the Champions League.

When Arsenal won the title last season, he also became the youngest player to lift the Premier League trophy.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incredible talent does not turn 17 until December 31 and will hope to get more run outs for Arsenal before then, although he has only had one very brief substitute appearance for the Gunners since his red card against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on October 27.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was clearly fuming with Dowman when he was shown a straight red card for reacting to a heavy challenge against Fleetwood, giving the youngster stern words as he left the field.

Arteta said: ‘I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘But, I don’t know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say “I don’t like the reaction”. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am.’

He added: ‘The reaction when I don’t win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time.

‘So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.’

#1888. Second-half blitz sinks Littlehampton as Eastbourne Borough reach Senior Cup last eight

A five-goal second half blitz underlined the Sports' superior status - but only after the Golds had turned around at half-time at 1-1 and with a glint of an upset in the gleaming, rain-soaked Priory Lane stadium.

George Gaskin and Mitch Hand's squad had made the long trek along the Sussex coast against the background of a frankly awful season so far. They’re a step lower than the Sports, but actually 44 places lower in terms of current league tables.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

And if it is ever possible to draw comfort from a 6-1 defeat, they can be satisfied this was a well contested game - which also banished memories of the two clubs' last encounter, an ill-tempered Senior Cup semi-final two seasons ago at Lancing.

Borough had thrown open the gates with free admission at the Connect Management Stadium - and those local football addicts who chose live footy ahead of a warm fireside were actually rather well rewarded.

Steve King's squad is strong on paper but stretched by injuries; but his line-up gave a starting shirt to FA Trophy hero Tyano Wilson as well as young reserve keeper Myles Watkins, and a place on the bench for patient striker Zack Tarrant - who would have the last word of the night.

Wilson created an early chance out of nothing, but his low cross flashed across goal with nobody able to convert. But on just seven minutes, the Sports were ahead: Arthur Grout played a perfectly weighted lofted pass to Liam Nash, who finished in style.

Cue a cascade of goals, through the silvery curtain of drizzle under gleaming lights? Nope - or at least not yet. Littlehampton kept their nerve, had a reasonable share of possession and kept their shape.

And, as the minutes drizzled away, half-time was suddenly approaching with the 1-0 scoreline unchanged. And just as suddenly, the Golds grabbed an equaliser through Marcel Powell - smartly taken if only just deserved on the balance of play.

With dressing room doors slammed tightly shut, King and his staff must have passed a few words of wisdom, and the second half saw a more determined and purposeful home performance.

In fact, it took just two minutes from the restart for Max Sheaf to restore the Sports' advantage with a beauty of a strike - and that set the second-half agenda.

Within five minutes, Myles-Watkins produced a strong save at his near post to deny Powell an equaliser. Then Gold Omotayo tucked one under the keeper to extend the home side's lead, or so they thought - but an offside flag chalked it off. No matter: Borough were now controlling most of the play.

Just past the hour, Laleye and Wilson combined beautifully at pace, to set up Gold's tap-in for 3-1. And three minutes later Owen Bellamy - often an unsung hero in the red Borough shirt - curled in the sweetest of strikes from 25 yards, to put the game effectively beyond Littlehampton's reach.

There was still time for Borough's strikers of the future to make their mark. Tarik Kadric and Tarrant enjoyed space against an understandably tiring visiting defence, and after Omotayo had converted a penalty for handball - furiously disputed by the visitors - it was Tarrant who claimed the final goal.

The tall youngster had too much pace for the Golds defence and his strike cannoned in off the underside of the bar.

For Littlehampton, a long and weary drive home, and that ever-ironic agenda to ‘concentrate on the league’. For the Sports, yet another victory - 20 in 22 games - and the ride rolls on.

#1887. BlueCo 'approach' Swansea City boss Vitor Matos to become Strasbourg manager

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 23:09

Strasbourg have reportedly made an approach for Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos.

The Welsh club have been one of the surprise packages of the EFL, with the Swans currently sitting in sixth position in the Championship table.

Matos has recorded a total of 22 wins, eight draws and 17 defeats across his 47 matches in all competitions.

However, despite penning a long-term contract at Swansea, it appears that the 38-year-old is prepared to leave for pastures new.

According to The Athletic, Strasbourg have identified Matos as a potential replacement for Portuguese compatriot Hugo Oliveira.

The 47-year-old left Famalicao to replace Gary O'Neil during the summer, the hope being that he could get Strasbourg back into Europe.

Instead, Strasbourg have accumulated just 10 points from as many matches to sit in 13th position in the Ligue 1 table.

While BlueCo are yet to make a final decision either way, they have seemingly lost faith in someone who guided Famalicao to fifth spot in Portugal's top flight in 2025-26.

Matos is said to be keen to take any opportunity that arises at Stade de la Meinau, putting his job at Swansea in doubt.

At this point in time, the assumption is that Matos will remain in charge for Swansea's Championship game versus West Bromwich Albion on Saturday afternoon.

With Strasbourg facing Brest, Le Havre, Lorient and Angers in their next four contests, Oliveira could be given at least some of that period to turn things around.

They remain just seven points behind fifth place, but they could finish the week in the relegation zone if results go against them in Ligue 1.

#1885. Jesus Owono’s punishment criticised following death of Jesus de Miguel

Andorra owner Gerard Pique says Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was announced that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the centre-forward’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated – and he died the following day.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the days and weeks that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Last week, Owono learned that he would be banned for Andorra’s next 12 matches for the role he played in the deadly collision, with the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee stating that the player had ‘violently struck an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

It went on: ‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

The statement added that the ‘nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances’ meant that the ‘maximum sanction’ was ‘justified’.

It was also confirmed that the match involving Andorra and Tenerife – which was called off when the teams were locked at 2-2 deep into stoppage time – would not be replayed.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred,’ it read.

Owono’s suspension has received a mixed reaction in Spain, with some feeling it too lenient while others have called for the ‘distressed’ goalkeeper to be given greater support.

According to Andorra owner Pique, the former Barcelona, Manchester United and Spain defender, Owono is ‘not to blame’ for the tragic outcome of the deadly collision.

‘I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve,’ he said in a statement.

‘He is not to blame for all of this having happened.’

Pique pointed to a separate incident earlier this month in Spanish football, when Albacete attacker Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell’s Quadri Liameed in the head during a second-tier encounter.

‘Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,’ Pique added.

‘With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?’

Pique, a World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, made it clear that Owono would likely require a significant break away from the game before being able to compete again.

‘Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to play,’ he continued.

‘No sanction is going to bring De Miguel back to us.’

Tenerife’s grieving squad returned to action for the first time since De Miguel’s death against Cueta on Sunday.

Goals from Nacho Gil and Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife a 2-0 victory on an emotional day the club’s Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

#1884. Chelsea and Manchester United lead race for Barcelona Fermin Lopez

By Alexis Pereira | 16 Nov 2026 23:37

Barcelona have reportedly received offers of up to £85m from the Premier League for Fermin Lopez, but the Spain midfielder wants to stay at Camp Nou and the club are preparing to discuss a new contract with his representatives. According to Sport, Chelsea and Manchester United are the two clubs most determined to sign the 23-year-old.

Long regarded as a promising player capable of bringing energy and drive off the bench, the attacking midfielder has gradually established himself as an important part of boss Hansi Flick’s system. His performances in recent months, particularly his two goals against Atletico Madrid, have strengthened his status further. At 23, he already has eight goals and seven assists in 15 appearances in all competitions this season.

His ability to get into the box, attack space from the second line and make a difference in the final 30 metres makes him a particularly valuable weapon for Barcelona. Lopez also brings strong intensity to the press and a verticality that complements the more organising midfielders in the Catalan squad. Unsurprisingly, the progress has not gone unnoticed in the transfer market, and several English clubs appear ready to invest heavily to persuade him to move.

According to Sport, Barcelona have received proposals from the Premier League for the attacking midfielder. Some reach £85m, a considerable amount that reflects the growing value of the Spain international, who has 12 caps. Chelsea and Manchester United are the two sides most determined to sign him, while the identity of the other two suitors has not been revealed.

Chelsea’s interest is not new. The London club tried in the last summer window with a proposal estimated at £59.5m, which did not even lead to real discussions with the Catalan hierarchy. This time the figures mentioned are much higher and leave Barcelona with an important decision to make.

From a sporting point of view, losing such a decisive and versatile player would be difficult to replace. Financially, however, a £85m fee could give interesting room for manoeuvre to a board that remains mindful of its economic constraints. It remains to be seen whether the club are genuinely willing to listen to such offers.

Barcelona’s main argument for keeping him may also be the most important: Lopez does not want to leave. He is strongly attached to the club, where he wants to keep progressing and put down roots, and he is not particularly tempted by approaches from the Premier League. The number seven has even said he wishes to end his career in Catalonia.

That position makes the sporting department’s job easier. According to Sport, Barcelona plan to meet his representatives soon to discuss a new contract improvement, with the aim of raising his salary to reflect his new status in Flick’s squad.

Lopez already extended his contract until 2031 in January 2026 and has a release clause of £425m. The Catalan club intend to keep protecting one of their most valuable assets, and in the face of the English millions, Barcelona seem to be considering a reward for their rising star rather than a departure.

“I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”

Mancini said that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team…

#1881. Gary Neville urges Mauricio Pochettino to sell five Manchester United players

Gary Neville has urged Mauricio Pochettino to sell five Manchester United players at the end of the season.

Pochettino has been brought in as Michael Carrick’s replacement and will arrive just three days before United’s next Premier League fixture away to Liverpool on November 22.

After a poor start to the season, United sit 18th in the Premier League with just one win in 10 games and are out of the Carabao Cup after a defeat at home to Brighton in September.

United’s players have been booed by supporters at Old Trafford but Neville believes Diogo Dalot has been made an ‘easy target’ and has defended the Portuguese full-back because of his work-rate.

Neville also feels Pochettino will look to move on Noussair Mazraoui, Matthijs de Ligt, Mason Mount, Marcus Rashford and Joshua Zirkzee at the end of the campaign, and expects Lisandro Martinez to leave when his contract expires next summer.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘Do I think Dalot is Denis Irwin? No. Let’s be really clear, Denis Irwin is the greatest full-back Manchester United have ever had, I shouldn’t be mentioning him in the same breath, but I would get rid of a few before Dalot,’ Neville said on Stick to United.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Dalot got booed last week at Old Trafford and I was really surprised at that. Dalot’s been shoved onto that left-hand side constantly. Amorim had him at left-wing back dying, it was awful to watch. If you put me at left wing-back or left-back, and I’m a right-back, by the way, and he’s a right-back, I’d be like, ‘not a chance, what are you putting me there for?’

‘So he’s literally sticking his hand up and saying, ‘go on, I’ll play there. I’ll do anything for the team.’ I never see him shirk anything, right? He’s not an amazing player, let’s be clear. He never shirks anything, him. I never look at him and think he could work harder. Ever.

‘I actually think, to be fair, if he was in a decent back four, he’d be all right. I actually do. But he’s got a shocking back four alongside him. Positionally he’s not great, he could be better on the ball. I just think he’s such an easy target, and I know that will be unpopular with the fanbase.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I’d be getting rid of Mazraoui well before him. I’d be getting rid of Martinez well before him. I’d be getting rid of De Ligt well before him.

‘De Ligt has got one big problem, he doesn’t play football. If a player is injury-prone and doesn’t play football, just because he hasn’t played it doesn’t mean he should go above a player who’s played every single week and is throwing his hand up.

‘You want someone who’s actually reliable and available to play. So De Ligt has to go.

‘I think he [Pochettino] will want to bring a new goalkeeper in. I think he’ll want someone to compete with [Senne] Lammens, I’m not saying he changes Lammens, I think it’s too early, I think we saw enough last season to carry on with him, hopefully build his confidence back up, I like his composure.

‘Out of the defenders he’ll keep [Luke] Shaw because he knows him and he’ll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries and you’ll have to manage him.

‘He’ll keep [Harry] Maguire because he’ll trust him and think he’s basically a soldier, someone who can do a job for him.

‘He’ll keep [Leny] Yoro because he’ll think there’s something to work with. [Ayden] Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in.

‘I’d keep Bruno [Fernandes], I’d keep Kobbie [Mainoo], I’d keep [Youri] Tielemans, Mount would have to go, [Andrey] Santos… Mauricio may like him because he’s young, quite mobile, he’s aggressive, he might get something out of him. Him and [Carlos] Baleba will be in that middle bit. Mount’s the one that goes definitely, in that midfield section.

‘Zirkzee definitely to go, I would think. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because of the fact he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, he’s in that section where you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.

‘He’ll work with Amad, he’ll work with Mbeumo, he’ll work with Cunha and he’ll work with Sesko and think, ‘okay, I’ll make you into a centre-forward’.

‘He’ll use Dorgu in the short term but he’ll be one who will go in the next couple of years. Ugarte will go, 100 per cent.

‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, De Ligt would go, Mazraoui would go, Mount would go, first wave next summer. Rashford if you can, and Zirkzee.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at Shaw, Maguire, Dalot, Bruno, that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on Baleba and Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’

#1880. Arsenal news: Declan Rice one of two Gunners stars to 'agree' terms over new contracts

By Ben Sully | 16 Nov 2026 23:52, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 04:08

Arsenal have reportedly reached an agreement with Declan Rice over a new long-term contract.

Rice is currently on the deal he signed when he arrived from West Ham in a £105m transfer in the summer of 2023.

That contract runs until June 2028, with an option to extend by a further 12 months, but his current terms are set to be replaced by a new deal.

The England international recently gave an update on his Arsenal future, revealing that a new deal will "hopefully be arriving soon".

As per The Athletic, Rice has now agreed a new five-year contract that will see him extend his Arsenal stay into the next decade, with an official confirmation expected in the near future.

The new contract will keep him at the Emirates Stadium for his peak years, given he will be 32 by the time the proposed deal expires in 2031.

The report suggests the terms of the deal will reflect Rice's status as an integral member of the Arsenal squad.

The 27-year-old has made 173 competitive appearances for the Gunners, contributing 22 goals and 36 assists.

Rice started 35 of his 36 league appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, as he played a key role in ending Arsenal's 22-year wait for Premier League glory.

The Englishman is not the only player who is set to sign fresh terms, with The Athletic reporting that Timber has agreed to a contract extension with the Gunners.

Timber's proposed new contract will see him extend his stay beyond the end of his current deal, which expires in the summer of 2028.

The Dutchman, who arrived from Ajax in 2023, featured regularly in Arsenal's title-winning campaign, chipping in with three goals and six assists in 30 Premier League appearances last term.

#1877. Gremio vs Bahia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 05:14

Gremio will host Bahia at their Arena do Gremio home in Porto Alegre on Wednesday night, for a crucial showdown that will have ramifications for both the Brasileirao's relegation battle and race for Copa Libertadores qualification.

The Tricolor dos Pampas are hoping to build on their cup success last time out, while the Steel Squad are keen to bounce back from defeat.

Renato Portaluppi's Gremio have endured a dire league campaign so far, but they are far from doomed in the Brazilian top flight.

The Tricolor dos Pampas held Athletico Mineiro to a 1-1 draw in the second leg of their Copa do Brasil semi-final on November 7, earning a 3-1 aggregate victory and a place in the final against Palmeiras.

In the Brasileirao, Portaluppi's side are currently 18th with 37 points to their name, sitting in the relegation zone with just four games to play.

However, Gremio are only one point shy of 16th-placed Internacional and 15th-placed Vitoria, giving the team genuine hope as the season enters its final stretch.

This week's hosts will also be buoyed by the fact they have lost just one of their last four home matches across all competitions, beating Mineiro 2-0 in the first leg of their cup tie after another 2-0 triumph over Athletico Paranaense in the league.

Meanwhile, Rogerio Ceni's Bahia are pushing for a place in the Copa Libertadores next term, and are currently in position to make the qualifiers, though the pressure is mounting.

The Steel Squad are sixth with 53 points, and with four matches remaining on their calendar, they sit one point short of fifth-placed Athletico Paranaense, and four behind fourth-placed Fluminense, who occupy one of the automatic entry spots.

That being said, Bahia's ambitions took a hit last time out on November 6, when they were downed 3-2 by Cruzeiro, who came from behind to win on a disappointing evening in Belo Horizonte.

As a result, Ceni's men are now within reach of seventh-placed Mineiro, who are a mere two points back in seventh after their goalless draw with Mirassol on Saturday.

To make matters worse, the visitors come into this clash having lost three of their past four away games, drawing once - a 1-1 stalemate with Santos late last month.

On the other hand, Bahia have played one match fewer than Mineiro, and Wednesday night represents a chance for them to strengthen their cushion over their rivals in the race for Libertadores qualification.

Gremio are without midfielders Mathias Villasanti (suspended), Juan Nardoni (thigh) and Danilo (muscle), though Dodi and Filip Krovinovic should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, Walter Kannemann is also suspended for accumulating yellow cards, while right-back options Diego Caito and Cristian Pavon are sidelined due to respective muscle injuries.

In their absence, Gustavo Martins, Wallace and Fabian Balbuena look set to start in a three-man defence, flanked by wing-backs Joao Pedro and Marlon.

As for Bahia, they are missing goalkeeper Leo Vieira, who is out for the season with a knee injury, while centre-half Marco Moreno is a doubt with stomach trouble.

If the latter is unavailable, then David Duarte and Kanu should be ready to start in front of shot-stopper Ronaldo.

Weverton; Martins, Wallace, Balbuena; Pedro, Dodi, Krovinovic, Marlon; Enamorado, Vinicius, Amuzu

Ronaldo; Victor, Duarte, Kanu, Juba; Erick, Acevedo, Nestor; Oliveira, Veliz, Pulga

Gremio may be in the relegation zone, but they arrive in better form than their opponents and will be optimistic about delivering a strong performance.

However, Bahia will be motivated by the race for Libertadores action, and are unlikely to be beaten again after their frustrating defeat last time out.

The Rovers boss, whose side makes the trip to Yorkshire rivals Bradford City on Saturday, said: "We don't really (talk about football). We just either go for something to eat or go out to the cinema or something like that and we just think about everything but (football) really.

"Just life and how he's getting on and all that sort of stuff.

"On most Thursday evenings, I'll take him out for a bit of food and just spend that little bit of time with him because I don't get to see him even though he's here every day.

"So we always go out and (usually) have something to eat. He's still hasn't paid yet!"

McCann's son (pictured) has made the breakthrough at first-team level this term at Rovers, having joined on a two-and-a-half year deal from South Yorkshire rivals Barnsley in the winter window.

The young midfielder, who turns 21 early next month, made his Rovers debut from the bench in the home game against Stevenage in late April.

He followed up with another substitute appearance at Peterborough United, a club both father and son know well, on the final day of the 2025-26 campaign.

McCann has kicked on this term, with his development recognised by an international call-up to Northern Ireland Under-21 side. He netted in the fixture against Malta in late September.

On the club front, McCann has made 13 appearances in all competitions for Rovers and scored his maiden goal for the club in the League One game at Luton Town on October 27.

According to reports, Glasgow Rangers recently sent scouts to monitor the form of McCann.

For McCann senior, it's very much business during working hours with his son, which is just the way that both want it.

He continued: "I want to be his manager when I'm in here and when we're away from here, I want to be his dad.

"That's just the relationship that we have and I think he prefers it like that.

"It's not like he gets any sort of special treatment or anything or I let him away (with anything).

"If anything, I'll probably speak to him less because I don't want to put any sort of pressure on him.

"I want him to just do his own thing. We still have phone calls now and again.

"He phoned me (recently) telling me his wi-fi was playing up at home, so me and my wife were trying to sort that out for him and it's things like that."

Bournemouth sensation Alex Scott should set his sights ‘higher’ than Chelsea and aim to join ‘one of the biggest teams in Europe’ like Arsenal.

That’s according to Chris Waddle, who claims Scott has taken his game ‘to a new level’ over the last 18 months and is looking more and more like the ‘complete’ central midfielder.

Waddle’s comments come amid mounting speculation over Scott’s future, with Bournemouth bracing themselves for incoming offers to steal their prized possession away in the January transfer window.

Scott’s eye-catching breakthrough in the international arena has done little to quieten rumours that the 23-year-old could soon be destined for bigger and better things, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham all rumoured to be circling.

Though Scott is currently sidelined with a thigh injury, his stock continues to soar – and it’s understood the Cherries could be prepared to do business should they receive a bid in excess of £80m this winter.

In an interview with iGaming.com, ex-England international Waddle revealed how he had been keeping close tabs on Scott’s progress since he was first alerted to his potential at Bristol City.

‘I’ve always liked Alex Scott. I think he’s a lovely, cultured player. There’s no doubt in my mind that in the last eighteen months, the kid’s taken his game to a new level,’ Waddle explained.

‘I followed him at Bristol City, and when he was there, I was speaking to someone that knew him who told me he was a Tottenham fan.

Chelsea are reportedly leading the hotly contested race to sign Scott and are said to be increasingly confident of reaching an agreement with Bournemouth for the central midfielder.

However, Waddle insists Scott should ideally be aiming higher than a move to Stamford Bridge, name-checking Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal as potential options.

‘According to reports, Chelsea retain the strongest interest in him. No disrespect to them, but I think he can look higher. I think he’s got the ability to play for the biggest teams in Europe: Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal,’ he added.

‘The guy looks like he’s a top player to me. He looks like he’s only going to get better. If I was a manager or a sporting director and I needed a midfielder, I would be looking at him.

‘He’s a complete midfielder. He can play as a 10, an 8, and a 6. He offers you a bit of everything. He reminds me a little bit of Rodri in the way that he likes to take the ball off the centre-back and start making things happen.

‘His composure and technique make him a standout player for any team looking to sign someone who can run a midfield and control the tempo.’

While Bournemouth are in no hurry to part with Scott, the club’s hierarchy recognise that the England international may have ambitions to move on elsewhere near future.

For now, though, the Cherries are adamant that the Vitality Stadium remains the ‘right place’ for Scott.

‘At this point, we’re convinced that we’re the right place for Alex to be, for Alex to stay, and we’ll keep on addressing contract issues with Alex as we move through this year,’ Bournemouth owner Bill Foley told talkSPORT last month.

‘We’d love to have Alex stay here, sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul, and we’re still working on it. We haven’t given up.

‘But sometimes players get stars in their eyes and they think that Chelsea is the right place to go or Manchester City.’

Scott’s current contract on the south coast runs through to June 2028.

“AC Milan’s transfer market is poised for significant events because Gerry Cardinale has no intention of stopping. His comments in recent days, both public and private, are a clear statement of what the AC Milan owner intends to do to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“Whether he succeeds or not will only be determined by time and the type of decisions he makes, but he certainly has the desire, vision, and financial resources. One can expect anything from someone who beat out Netflix for the Warner Bros. acquisition.

“Among the many things he has learned is that the climate of mediocrity surrounding results has undermined the mentality of a club and an environment that, instead, must strive to always be at the top.

“But returning to those levels requires several factors: a clear decision-making structure (which will be finalised by Markus Krösche, who will always report to Cardinale, who will always have the final say and be involved in negotiations), strong players in the squad, a political presence in the halls of power, a connection with the fans, and credibility.

“What may seem like slogans in themselves are actually manifestos that one can legitimately believe or not. The only way to evaluate Cardinale’s work is to observe how he operates and then draw conclusions.

“He’s fired up, and between January and next summer there will be some serious transfer campaigns. The reason is simple: there’s a need to significantly raise the squad’s level, creating a core of 16-18 players of a certain caliber who can be joined by young players to develop and develop.

“This is why Milan will be looking for not only technically strong players, but also leaders who can complement those already in the Milan core group.

“It’s crucial to raise the team’s personality, including strong personalities who can provide a different kind of motivation during the day-to-day at Milanello. These players, inevitably, cost money, but Cardinale doesn’t want to set limits.

“This doesn’t mean Milan will sign a player worth one hundred million euros, but it does mean they can continue along the operational path laid out by Diego Moreira. All of this is in concert and in line with Ruben Amorim, who is fiercely defended by the AC Milan owner and with whom he intends to begin a long-term relationship.

“And the vision is to acquire the Van Dijks in the pre-prime phase rather than signing them at 35 (assuming, for the sake of argument, that I’d sign someone like that now).

“In my opinion, a Sandro Tonali- style signing is needed. And it’s not out of the question that Milan could try to bring him back in the coming years, even though he currently plays for a club as complex to negotiate with as Tottenham.

“Meanwhile, discussions are ongoing to finalise the renewal of Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse.”

#1869. Trey Nyoni names Arsenal star as ‘toughest opponent’

Liverpool youngster Trey Nyoni has picked out Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard as the ‘toughest opponent’ he has faced at the start of his career.

Odegaard has returned to his sparkling best this season, starting all ten of Arsenal’s opening matches in the Premier League with the reigning champions sitting five points clear at the summit.

Having managed just one goal across the Gunners’ title-winning campaign last term, the 27-year-old appears to have rediscovered his scoring boots, finding the net on five occasions in all competitions this term.

It was Odegaard’s 72nd-minute strike that proved the difference before the international break, when Mikel Arteta’s men were made to work for their victory at home to newly promoted Hull City.

The Norway international will no doubt be desperate to pick up where he left off when the north London giants return to top-flight against at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Nyoni has himself enjoyed an impressive start to the season at Liverpool and locked horns with Odegaard when the pair did battle at Anfield at the start of the month.

And while Nyoni was taken off before the hour-mark on Merseyside, it’s clear Odegaard left a big impression on the 19-year-old in the 58 minutes his opposite number was on the pitch.

Asked to name the ‘toughest’ player he has come up against, Nyoni told The Inside Scoop, ‘For me personally, I would say Odegaard,’ as he looked back on that afternoon.

‘The way he plays, it’s very busy, moving around and always looking for an option.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s not easy as a midfielder. I think when you play against someone who is constantly moving, you know in the back of your mind that he could be here, but the next minute he’s there.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

When asked if Odegaard perhaps doesn’t get the credit he deserves, Nyoni replied: ‘Yeah, I think the game is evolving and I think nowadays people look at No.10s and automatically think that if they’re not getting goals and assists, they’re not good.

‘For example, in our team we’ve got Flo [Wirtz]. I think Flo does a lot of stuff that people don’t really see.

‘I think what he brings to the team benefits the team. Just because he’s not scoring or assisting, doesn’t mean he’s not effective.

‘Nowadays, the idea that if a player isn’t getting goals or assists, they’re useless, but every player has their own role in the team.

‘Odegaard and people like Flo, if they’re not getting goals and assists, people that don’t watch the game automatically think they haven’t played well but that’s not how football works.’

In the aftermath of Arsenal’s nervy win over Hull, club legend Paul Merson said Odegaard had been ‘like a new signing’ for Arteta this season.

‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it quickly,’ Merson said of Odegaard on Sky Sports.

‘He moves it quickly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance.

‘I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far.

‘Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show.’

#1867. Derby agendas for Barnsley FC, Bradford City, Doncaster Rovers, Huddersfield Town and Sheffield Wednesday

Barnsley and Doncaster Rovers - down among the dead men in League One - will be hoping that rings true as they seek precious shafts of light following arduous autumns.

They face back-to-back derbies in their next two fixtures, which will assume importance not just for the morale of each club, but also for Daniel Stendel and Grant McCann in their second spells at the Reds and Rovers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sheffield Wednesday, Bradford City and Huddersfield Town have their own motivations to contend with.

In the second half of last autumn, Barnsley slipped up at home to Rotherham United, who won in the league at Oakwell for the first time in 15 visits since March 1969. But they did afford themselves the fillip of three points at Doncaster 14 days later.

The Reds, who welcome the Owls on Friday before visiting Bradford - managed by ex-boss Michael Duff - next Tuesday, would probably settle for a 50 per cent derby ratio this time around.

More especially given that their grim winless league run - nine matches and counting - has descended into a crisis.

They must make do without top-scorer and suspended captain Cameron McGeehan on Friday, while defender Jack Shepherd, a boyhood Wednesdayite, is also banned. The return of Patrick Kelly from international duty with Northern Ireland is a much more welcome development.

The sight of in-form Owls striker and Reds old boy Davis Keillor-Dunn compounding their autumnal angst certainly wouldn't be.

A match-winning display from DKD - who has struck in his last three Wednesday matches - would put the tinlid on things for Reds followers, whose expectation levels are exceedingly low heading into Friday.

If things turn sour, the mood in the home stands has the potential to turn mutinous towards the club hierarchy. Barnsley are without a league win since September 2 and are only kept off the bottom of the table by goal difference. A protest from fans group Tykes Union is planned beforehand.

Derbies brought out the best in McCann's Rovers in League One last season and their recent 2-0 win over Wednesday keeping to that theme.

Rovers secured a derby double against arch-rivals Rotherham for the first time since 1949-50 and made history by winning league games at Barnsley and Millers in the same season.

McCann's side also beat Town and Bradford at home and performed very well in both away games and were extremely unlucky to lose both.

They visit the Bantams on Saturday, seeking to get back onside with supporters following dreadful away performances in their last two matches in league and cup - an embarrassing 3-0 FA Cup loss at non-league Kidderminster and an equally atrocious 6-1 league beating at MK Dons.

On both occasions, McCann issued an apology to travelling fans with some starting to openly question his future. The Rovers chief, whose side host high-flying Town next Thursday, prides himself as being a fighter.

Wednesday’s derby form this term has been in keeping with their wretched numbers on that count over the past couple of years.

They have won just once in their past 14 league fixtures against White Rose counterparts.

So far this season, they were bullied in the second half of their meeting with Bradford in their opening home league fixture of 2026-27 - a 1-0 defeat which was more emphatic than the scoreline sounded.

By common consent, they were somewhat fortunate to secure a late point at Huddersfield on October 10 - when Town were very much the architects of their own downfall.

A fortnight later, a disjointed, unsatisfactory performance at Doncaster proved the final straw for the Owls hierarchy regarding Henrik Pedersen.

Historically, Oakwell at least provides rather happier memories for the Owls, notwithstanding their last visit. They have lost just once on their last eight trips up the A61.

After dismal displays - not just results - in three derby losses at Valley Parade, the Club Doncaster Sports Village and Oakwell last season, redressing the balance would be a barometer of Town’s progress in 26-27.

It’s a case of so far, so good with the Terriers avenging last season’s anaemic loss at Bradford with a cathartic victory on Hallowe’en. Statistically speaking, the visitors’ 3-0 triumph was their biggest ever at BD8.

They have two other scores to settle. Town were fitful in their 3-1 defeat at Oakwell last August and it was a sign of things to come for ex-head coach Lee Grant. They visit Barnsley on December 19.

There were jeers and opprobrium following a tepid 1-0 reverse in Doncaster on a February night when Town’s top-six pitch was exposed.

The present-day worries belong to Rovers. And Barnsley.

#1865. Liverpool injury news: Reds receive fresh Dominik Szoboszlai update ahead of Man United clash

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 00:33

Hungary boss Marco Rossi has insisted Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai is fit to play in Tuesday's UEFA Nations League clash against Northern Ireland.

Szoboszlai was forced off with a minor knee issue in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

As a result, there was some doubt as to whether he would link up with the Hungary squad for the final two matches of the Nations League league phase.

Not only did he join up with his national team, but he played the full duration of Saturday's 2-0 away win over Georgia, in which he provided an assist for Barnabas Varga's 85th-minute effort.

Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he was close to pulling out of the game after feeling the injury in the pre-match warm-up.

The midfielder also said his leg "felt good" during the game and that he would start the "treatment process all over again" in a bid to be ready for Tuesday's home meeting with Northern Ireland.

Speaking in Monday's pre-match press conference, Rossi attempted to ease fears over Szoboszlai's injury status, insisting his captain is ready to feature at the Puskas Arena.

“Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?” Rossi said.

“I didn’t see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available.

“I don’t think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don’t think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia.”

For Hungary, Tuesday's game is an important fixture as it offers the chance to secure promotion to League A of the Nations League.

Having collected 10 points from their five matches, Hungary enter the final matchday in second spot and one point behind leaders Northern Ireland in Group B2.

Meanwhile, Liverpool's main priority is Sunday's Premier League clash against Manchester United, who will start life under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will be keen to have Szoboszlai available for the home fixture, especially as there is doubt over Ryan Gravenberch's availability.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has spent the bulk of the last decade as England’s first choice but is being pushed hard by Trafford.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Playing time has been evenly split between the pair across the last two international breaks and Trafford was given the gloves against Spain on Sunday (November 15).

He delivered a stellar display in the 3-2 Nations League win, intensifying calls for him to replace Pickford as the number one.

Gerrard told The Overlap Daily: “I really like Trafford, I think he’s the future. But I also like Pickford. I don’t think we can sit here after one performance and dismiss Pickford.

“We’ve probably got two England number ones and the manager’s just got the big decision and that’s why he gets the big bucks. But the future’s Trafford. I think that’s healthy.

“I don’t like it when it’s just a foregone conclusion. He’s the England number one and it doesn’t matter how he plays because he’s the outright number one. Why can’t there be competition, why can’t there be healthy competition?”

Trafford produced a stunning double save in the dying embers, enabling England to hang on and secure a valuable victory over the reigning world champions.

Gerrard said: “It made us win the game. It’s as good or as important as a goal. The second save is world class. There was also a shot straight after it which bounced just in front of him on a greasy surface and it was just like velcro.

“It just stuck to his body. I was really impressed with that as well. It looked simple on the TV but you see so many goalkeepers spill them or want to push them away. He’s just like velcro.”

#1862. Mauricio Pochettino is CONFIRMED as new Man United manager: Departing USA boss speaks out as he agrees to succeed Michael Carrick - but faces race against time for first game

Published: 07:02 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 07:51 EST, 13 November 2026

Manchester United have confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become their new head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will replace Michael Carrick who was sacked following 10 months in charge on Friday, after United agreed to pay more than £10million to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his new job as United boss on Wednesday. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

There were no comments from Pochettino or United officials in Friday’s press release confirming his appointment because he remains contracted to US Soccer.

Pochettino said in the USMNT's statement: 'The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honors of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.'

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday, but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week.

United sources say that Pochettino’s experience, philosophy, personality and skill-set make him well suited for the job, as well as his record of developing individual talent and building excellent team cultures.

Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as the Manchester United manager

Michael Carrick was sacked after the club made their worst start to the season in 40 years

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’

Earlier in the week, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am on Thursday morning and was dismissed.

He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He became the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season.

United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

'His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'

Sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick indicated.

United feel that the squad are far better than their position in the Premier League shows

They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

It has been a campaign in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and they are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league.

Pochettino's United travel to Anfield on November 22 before a Champions League clash at Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino's first home game against Brentford and then away match at Newcastle.

Carl Ikeme has fondly recalled his loan spell at Middlesbrough - and believes anything but automatic promotion this season would be disappointing for the club.

He spent time at Middlesbrough during the 2011/12 season and made 10 appearances during the reign of Tony Mowbray.

A number of the 40-year-old’s former clubs are in the Championship promotion race, therefore it is something he is keeping a close eye on.

“I think there’s some strong teams,” he told The Yorkshire Post. “I think out of the teams that were left in the Championship, they (Middlesbrough) were the standout team.

#1859. Max Dowman achieves historic England Under-21s feat as Arsenal youngster breaks another Jude Bellingham record

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 04:00

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goalscorer in Monday's 3-2 win over France.

After making 13 appearances for England's Under-19 side, Dowman earned his first call-up to the Under-21 squad for the current international window.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player to represent England Under-21s when he featured as a substitute in the 1-0 defeat against Portugal in Friday's friendly at Ashton Gate, surpassing the record previously held by Jude Bellingham.

Dowman was then given the chance to start Monday's friendly against France, and he made the most of his opportunity, scoring an 89th-minute winner after England had spurned a two-goal lead.

The winning goal ✨ Max Dowman has his first goal for our #YoungLions! https://t.co/gb4rLaXXBV

Everton's Harrison Armstrong created the winner, stealing possession high up the pitch before squaring the ball for Dowman to steer home a simple left-foot finish.

As a result of the effort, Dowman took another record away from Bellingham as he became England Under-21s' youngest-ever scorer.

Dowman found the net at the age of 16 years and 320 days old, surpassing the record Bellingham set when he scored on his Under-21s debut against Kosovo at the age of 17 years and 67 days in September 2020.

The Arsenal academy product also picked up the Player of the Match award as he helped Carsley's side end a three-game winless run.

The winning goal and your #YoungLions Player of the Match connected by @EE! ? Max Dowman ? https://t.co/eNmPkLLWVN

In regard to the England Under-21s, Dowman will hope to be part of the squad that heads to Albania and Serbia next summer for the European Under-21 Championship.

In the short term, the winger will link back up with his Arsenal teammates, who will prepare for Saturday's Premier League away clash against Newcastle United.

However, he will be unable to feature against the Magpies as he serves the final match of the three-game ban he received following his red card in the EFL Cup defeat against Fleetwood Town.

Dowman could return to the squad for the Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund on November 24, just days before the Gunners take on Manchester City in the Premier League.

#1857. Leeds United midfielder Sean Longstaff lifts lid on ‘tough year’ and makes Newcastle United comparison

Leeds United midfielder Sean Longstaff has conceded his move to Elland Road has not gone completely to plan.

The 29-year-old signed for the Whites as part of their post-promotion recruitment drive in the summer of 2025, making a £12m move from his boyhood club Newcastle United.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He started his maiden campaign as a midfield regular but missed the weeks in which Leeds turned their season around through injury.

Opportunities were limited upon his return and competition in the middle of the park has only intensified in his second season.

He told The Official Leeds United Podcast: “I’d be lying if I said it’s been the easiest year I’ve ever had. It’s been a tough year.

“There’s probably been times, at home, especially, there’s times where you’re not that nice to be around. Ultimately, I made the decision to come to Leeds. I took my family away from the comforts of being at their home. I’ve took a newborn baby away from his grandparents to bring him down here for me to enhance my career.

“Obviously, at the minute, it’s not gone probably to the perfect plan. But I don’t think life ever does.”

Longstaff was handed his first league start of the season before the international break, completing 90 minutes in Leeds’ 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur.

He made his 200th Premier League appearance in the game and the reaching of the milestone in such a valuable win served as a reward for his perseverance.

The midfielder said: “For me, I take training as serious as possible. Whether that’s the day after a game, whether it’s during the week, you’ve got to train as if you’re going to play.

“And then ultimately, if you don’t play, that’s not in my control. I can’t control it. All I can control is, make sure I’m fit enough to play when I get a chance, make sure I’m sharp enough, make sure my mentality is right.

“If I get a chance, I want to try and show what I can do, whether that’s for 30 seconds whether that’s a for, come on at half-time, or whatever the case may be. I can’t control other people’s decisions. All I can control is the controllables.”

Longstaff may not have seen the level of action he wanted in West Yorkshire, but has spoken of the club with great affection.

He has compared the Whites to Newcastle, who he made 214 appearances for before departing.

He said: “It’s still close to home so it didn’t feel like you were moving away miles. It’s not until you probably get down here, everyone says Leeds is a massive club, but until you get here, you don’t realise how big it is.

“I came with an expectation of ‘it’s going to be Newcastle’s this and Leeds is that’. Then you get in, you think ‘oh actually, Leeds is so similar.

“Apart from the kit, everything else felt exactly the same. Obviously the only difference is me being from Newcastle and not from Leeds, but actually got to know a lot of people from the city and they were telling us stuff. The way they speak about Leeds is the way I felt about Newcastle. The more you meet people, the more you realise it’s massive.”

#1855. Premier League panel confirm ruling on Kai Havertz incident in Hull City’s defeat to Arsenal

Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty in their 1-0 win over Hull City before the international break, a Premier League panel have ruled.

Martin Odegaard struck the decisive goal for the Gunners, who played host to the Tigers on November 7.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hull were widely lauded for their defensive grit in the game, although the division’s key match incidents panel has claimed they should have been penalised.

Tigers defender Nobel Mendy held on to Gunners forward Kai Havertz yet even after a VAR review, a spot-kick was not awarded.

The panel said: “Although Harvertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz.

“Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded.

“The panel consdered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.”

Arsenal will not feel too aggrieved given they secured three points, but it would most likely have been a different story had they not.

Reflecting on the game, Tigers defender John Egan told the club’s media team: “I feel like we put a really good performance in, put a lot into the game. You know, what we worked on all week, we put on the pitch. Maybe [it was] a little bit of a missed opportunity the way we played.

“I think we deserved a result. We made it hard for them. [I’m] proud of the lads. I really thought we played really well, so mixed feelings. Disappointed not to get a result, but also a really tough place to come. We played really well.

#1852. Seattle Sounders vs Real Salt Lake - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 17 Nov 2026 02:48

The final playoff game on the Western Conference side will take place Thursday as the Seattle Sounders host Real Salt Lake in the MLS Wild Card Round at Lumen Field.

These teams wound up eighth and ninth in the West during the regular season, with the Rave Green defeating Los Angeles FC the last time out 2-1, putting them a point above Salt Lake, who won by that same score on Decision Day against the Los Angeles Galaxy.

It was an underwhelming regular season overall for Seattle, but they managed to get a result when needed to keep their campaign alive.

While they finished with nine fewer points this year than in 2025, Brian Schmetzer’s men found a way to stay above the playoff line by the skin of their teeth.

They have dropped points in five of their last six games but have won more playoff encounters than any MLS club (26) since their debut season in the league in 2009.

In 2026, the Sounders lost four more home games (five) than the year before, though they have only lost one playoff match at Lumen Field this decade in normal time, with Los Angeles FC blanking them 1-0 in 2023.

This will be the first time they compete in the Wild Card Round, with the Rave Green winning their first post-season home outing in 2025.

The Sounders are unbeaten in their last four MLS home games versus Real Salt Lake, collecting a clean sheet on three of those occasions.

Like Seattle, Salt Lake came up big when needed on Decision Day, qualifying for the post-season for a sixth consecutive time.

While Pablo Mastroeni has never missed the playoffs since taking charge of this team in 2021, they lost their only Wild Card outing last year at the Portland Timbers (3-1).

On Thursday, RSL will try to end a four-match playoff losing run and win their first post-season game away from home since upsetting Sporting Kansas City 2-1 in 2021.

During the 2026 MLS campaign, Claret and Cobalt were pointless in their three away outings against the Cascadia clubs (the Portland Timbers, Vancouver Whitecaps and Sounders), netting just one goal overall against those teams.

Entering this must-win game, however, the club from Sandy, Utah have won two of their last three MLS away encounters.

Their recent playoff form may not be great, but RSL have won their last two knockout matches against Seattle across all competitions, upsetting them on penalties at Lumen Field in the opening round of the 2021 MLS Cup playoffs.

Seattle Sounders Major League Soccer form:

Both Alex Roldan and Danny Musovski will be questionable for the Sounders on Thursday, with the former recovering from a calf strain and the latter from a head injury.

A knee problem will likely keep Nikola Petkovic out as well, while Yeimar Gomez Andrade has a sore hamstring and Pedro de la Vega is doubtful with a quad issue.

Albert Rusnak and Sebastian Gomez netted first-half goals which were ultimately just enough to earn them a win against LAFC.

As for Real Salt Lake, Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are both unlikely to feature in this upcoming fixture due to knee injuries.

There were several new faces in their starting 11 on Decision Day, with Kobi Henry and Zach Booth among those being inserted on the backline.

Sergi Solans and Booth found the back of the net early versus the Galaxy, while an own goal from Luc de Fougerolles led to some anxious moments in the second half before the final whistle blew.

Seattle Sounders possible starting lineup:
