#1850. Orlando City vs FC Cincinnati - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 17 Nov 2026 02:52, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 18:26

With a spot in the opening phase of the MLS Cup playoffs up for grabs, Orlando City will welcome FC Cincinnati to Inter.com Stadium in the Sunshine State on Thursday for that Wild Card matchup.

The Lions finished the regular season eighth, blanking the New England Revolution 1-0 in their last meeting, with Cincy below them after a 2-0 Decision Day home defeat to Nashville SC.

A season that appeared headed for disaster in the spring came to life in the late summer as Orlando City recovered and climbed back above the playoff line.

The arrival of Antoine Griezmann changed their fortunes dramatically, with nine of this club’s 13 wins coming after the 2018 World Cup winner joined.

Martin Perelman’s men are unbeaten in their last seven MLS outings at home, dropping points on only one of those occasions.

On Thursday they can collect their first post-season triumph since the 2024 Eastern Conference semi-finals, when they blanked Atlanta United 1-0.

Orlando have won six straight league contests at home when netting the opening goal and have never lost a playoff game on home soil when doing so.

Thanks in part to Griezmann’s presence, the Lions rose to eighth in the league regarding average goals per game (1.9) in 2026.

In a win-and-in scenario on Decision Day, Cincinnati failed to deliver, ending a four-match domestic unbeaten run and setting up this Wild Card showdown.

A defeat on Thursday would mark the first time that the Orange and Blue fail to feature in the first round of the playoffs since Pat Noonan took charge ahead of the 2022 campaign.

Cincinnati have points in three successive MLS away encounters and have lost just one of their last five games domestically as the visitors.

They have never won a post-season away game in 90 minutes, with their only such triumph occurring in New Jersey in 2023 on penalties versus the New York Red Bulls.

They averaged the fourth-most goals per match in the league this past season (2.0) but conceded the third-most per game (2.2) just slightly fewer than Orlando City, who were second from the bottom in that department (2.3).

The Orange and Blue are unbeaten in their last four MLS meeting versus Orlando City, while Noonan has never lost a match against them at Inter.co Stadium.

Due to a back injury, Griffin Dorsey is questionable for Orlando City, while foot issues are likely to keep Tyrese Spicer and Robin Jansson out of the fold on Thursday and Iago Teodoro is eligible to return from his suspension.

Braian Ojeda had the only goal against New England on Decision Day while Maxime Crepeau collected his fifth clean sheet of the campaign.

On the Cincinnati side, Julian Malatini is doubtful due to a leg injury, while Nick Hagglund is unlikely to clear concussion protocol and Obinna Nwobodo is out because of a yellow card suspension.

Tom Barlow became just the second Cincy player to appear in all 34 regular-season outings the last time out, while Evander had double digits in goals and assists in 2026, finishing tied for second in the league with Lionel Messi in regular-season assists (17).

Crepeau; Taifi, Brekalo, Cartagena, Nogueira; Pasalic, B. Ojeda, Atuesta, Angulo; Griezmann, Dike

Celentano; Smith, Hadebe, Robinson; Martinez, Bucha, Evander, Anunga, Ramirez; Denkey, Barlow

#1849. Alfie Whiteman interview: Life is short, I left Tottenham and football to experience the world

From the Europa League final to the Prince Charles Cinema, the former goalkeeper is carving out a new career

Trawl through Alfie Whiteman’s most recent Instagram post, and you will stumble across a fridge cluttered with magnets, polaroid pictures and a Europa League winners medal.

There, hidden within a carousel of charity shops, cameras and cats, lies a perfectly understated summation of where football figures for a man who cut short his professional career at just 26, not through injury or mental distress, but to pursue a passion for the arts.

Whiteman spent 16 years as a goalkeeper at his boyhood club, Tottenham, but he admits he has not been back to watch them live since hanging up his gloves in October last year.

“I had an offer,” Whiteman tells Standard Sport after taking part in a live Q&A for the launch of Together Tottenham - a new shared mission between the club and Spurs in the Community to create 150,000 meaningful opportunities for local young people by 2030.

Life is short, and I wanted to make sure I experienced the other wonderful things the world has to offer

“I could have continued to play, but I think for many years prior I was always planning for life after (football).

“Life is short, and I wanted to make sure I experienced the other wonderful things the world has to offer, but it was a huge decision that came with a lot of self-doubt and risk because there wasn’t something set up for me to look into.”

Whiteman stepped into the unknown in pursuit of his “purpose beyond the sport”. But it is a decision he is grateful he took after years spent living a “double life” in which his creative instincts were “discouraged”.

Physically and metaphorically, he had closed the door on his football career, locking away his Europa League and 2019 Champions League runners-up medal in a drawer before eventually putting them pride of place alongside pictures of his friends and family.

He continued: “It’s funny. For a long time they (the medals) were just in a drawer, but I thought I’d put them out as a reminder for me of all the wonderful experiences that my life and football gave me and how hard I worked.

“My whole childhood was essentially devoted to battling my way through the footballing system, which famously is not an easy one to go through.”

Whiteman only ever made one senior competitive appearance for Spurs, coming on as an 82nd-minute substitute for Joe Hart in a 4–0 Europa League win against Ludogorets Razgrad in November 2020.

However, his connection to the club remains strong, and he admits the 2025 Europa League triumph against Manchester United, which ended Spurs’ 17-year wait for a major trophy, was the perfect send-off.

“I look back on it as the best possible final game, running on that pitch and celebrating with my wonderful teammates and all the work we put in through a tricky year.”

Despite winning the Europa League, it was a complicated campaign for Spurs, as they slumped to their worst ever Premier League season, finishing 17th and losing 22 of their 38 league games.

Spurs dropped everything to end their trophy drought, and manager Ange Postecoglu paid with his job, sacked 16 days after the final despite staying true to his promise to deliver silverware in his second season.

Simultaneously “within and without” as the Great Gatsby narrator, Nick Carraway, once famously quipped, Whiteman held a unique position in Spurs’ squad during his final season.

People think they know a lot about [football] but the reality of it within the walls of the training ground is probably quite different

He was aware he was never likely to influence the game on the pitch, yet understood he had a role to play in the dressing room and on the training ground as they stood on the cusp of history.

“I do feel football is something that people think they know a lot about but the reality of it within the walls of the training ground is probably quite different,” Whiteman asserts. “Everyone wins together and suffers together.”

Retirement was already in Whiteman’s plans as he rushed onto the pitch in Bilbao. Four years earlier, he captured over 600 vulnerable self-portraits and diary entries that encapsulated the solitude, loneliness, and self-exploration of his loan spell with Swedish club Degerfors IF.

These insights would form the basis of his first formal step into the arts, as his exhibition ‘A Loan’ was showcased at the OOF Gallery inside the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

“It wasn’t a project made with the idea of it being exhibited. It was purely out of this time of searching for purpose, frustration with self, feeling like I’m down a path that maybe isn’t the one I want to do and dealing with insecurities and imposter syndrome.

“It was just reflecting upon all those things of self-doubt, so it was quite surreal, actually. It was nice that it was resonating with people.”

Influenced by his parents, who were always “encouraging art and expression”, and his upbringing in cosmopolitan London, Whiteman is also a major film buff and regularly heads to the BFI Southbank or the Prince Charles Cinema in Leicester Square.

He recently attended the BFI’s London Film Festival, where the comedy-drama Club Kid was among the screenings to catch his attention. If there was one film to sum up his time at Spurs, though?

“Wow, that’s a tricky question,” he chuckles before a clinical concentration becomes etched across his face as if stepping up to save the winning penalty in the World Cup final.

“Wim Wenders’ (1987 romantic fantasy) Wings of Desire but maybe (Wenders’ 2023 Japanese-language drama) Perfect Days, one of his more recent films.

“I think (in Perfect Days) it was this real appreciation of life itself and the small things, and not getting caught up in all the stresses we have and just taking a step back and appreciating how lucky we are, which I think that film really encapsulates.

“It’s about really finding purpose in what you’re doing, and that sort of beauty of the small everyday things.”

#1848. Mikel Arteta has Arsenal stars looking as hungry as ever with rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal hold a five-point lead at the top of the Premier League table.

A 3-0 loss at the Amex Stadium against Brighton was the only one of their ten matches so far this season in which they have dropped points in the league.

With 10 points from a possible 12 in the Champions League as well, it has been near enough as good a start as Mikel Arteta and his players could have wished for.

The defeat away at Brighton was a horror show and the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood was embarrassing, but otherwise it was a superb start to the season for Arsenal.

They have, on the whole, played better football than last season, even if many matches have not had the margin to make it feel more comfortable.

Arsenal went toe-to-toe with Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena, a performance that should give them real confidence when the knockout stages of the Champions League come around.

It has been a tough run of fixtures to start the season, with so many difficult away trips already ticked off, and Arsenal have come through that sitting pretty.

Ezri Konsa has been by far the standout of the summer additions. He has slotted into the defence seamlessly and made an already formidable backline look effectively impenetrable.

There can be no greater compliment to Konsa than the fact he has given Arteta a major selection headache now William Saliba is fit again.

Bruno Guimaraes' best moments have come off the bench, with goals against Sunderland and Leeds. He has thrived when things have been more desperate and there is a chaotic edge to the match.

When starting alongside Declan Rice, Guimaraes has looked far less comfortable and his lack of mobility has been exposed on several occasions.

Further up the pitch, Christos Tzolis made a bright start to life at the club before missing a month with a hamstring injury.

It is still hard not to look at the summer transfer window as a huge missed opportunity in attack. Arsenal needed to do much more.

Konsa aside, it feels like the form this season is in spite of the business done in that window rather than because of it.

He did not get the statement attacking signing he wanted in the summer but Mikel Arteta has not let that slow Arsenal down.

After the mental and physical toll last season took on the squad, followed by many of them spending the summer at the World Cup, there was a strong chance that Arsenal could have stumbled into the new season.

That has not happened. Arteta has got his players looking as hungry as ever and the start to the league campaign has been brilliant.

The one criticism of Arteta would still be how he manages certain players. He has rotated this season, particularly in Europe, but it still feels as though unnecessary risks are sometimes taken.

Did Declan Rice need to play 90 minutes against Slavia Prague, for example? Gabriel, too, is surely in need of a rest soon.

I backed Arsenal to defend their crown in the summer and see no reason to change that stance now.

With the uncertainty surrounding Manchester City, and the likes of Chelsea and Liverpool looking extremely unconvincing, Arsenal are by far the club in the best shape to win the title again.

#1846. Man United transfer news: Two Nico Paz demands could rule out Red Devils move

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:14

Midfielder Nico Paz could leave Como in 2027, and Manchester United are mentioned as a possible destination for the Argentine. But he has demands that could be problematic for the club.

Author of a fine season with his club so far - 14 matches, six goals and eight assists - the 22-year-old attacking midfielder is already setting the 2027 transfer market alight. Real Madrid are the favourites to bring him back, thanks to their £68m (€80m) buy-back clause, but PSG could still take advantage, while Manchester United are thinking of Paz as a dream replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

But the expectations of the 15-cap international for his future club could mean Paris disappear from the equation.

According to information shared by The Touchline, Paz has two demands for the rest of his career and his future club.

The first is that the club in question play in the Champions League, and do so consistently. That could rule out Manchester United, as the English club, who have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, are currently 18th in the Premier League.

The second is a guarantee of a place in the starting XI. Here it is with PSG that this could weigh: as Luis Enrique has repeated on several occasions in the past, the two-time European champions do not promise any player a place in the starting XI.

All the more so as the Spanish manager readily practises rotation, even if some players are obviously more regular starters than others.

Still young (22), Paz left Real Madrid in 2024 to make a name for himself in Italy and then in Europe with Como.

Very early on, then, the Argentine put playing time ahead of everything else: a move to Como could represent a sporting gamble, as the Italian club, although backed by a billionaire, had just been promoted to Serie A.

For the rest of his career, therefore, the playmaker intends to be attentive to his playing time, even if his talent, now recognised, naturally opens doors for him.

But not necessarily those of PSG, where competition is fierce in attack and in midfield. The same goes for Real Madrid: can Como’s number 10 oust Jude Bellingham as the central attacking midfielder at Real? Not so sure... Could that also call into question a possible future in Madrid?

#1845. Why the jury remains out on Xabi Alonso despite Chelsea progress with rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have made progress under Xabi Alonso in some areas but in others still look the same chaotic team Enzo Maresca and then Liam Rosenior presided over.

They sit fifth in the table at present and boast one of the Premier League’s most thrilling attacks yet have also dropped points against Hull and lost to both Tottenham and Sunderland, who were bottom of the table at the time.

As the November international break draws to a close, it is time to reassess the progress they have made and the direction of travel under Alonso.

Chelsea’s season began with strong form but in truth has very much been a mixed bag so far.

The victories over Fulham, Brighton, Bournemouth and Leeds (in the Carabao Cup) have shown Chelsea at their free-flowing best, but only twice have they kept a Premier League clean sheet so far and there are defensive weaknesses that either need solving or, failing that, disguising by Alonso and his team in the months ahead.

The penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool that saw Chelsea exit the Carabao Cup early was a real disappointment in a season when there is no European football to be had, and it is understandable why plenty of Chelsea fans remain unsure quite what Alonso’s team are and what they want to be, even though they sit fifth in the league.

They have been beaten by Tottenham and Sunderland, neither of which should be games they are losing.

Chelsea made 10 first-team signings in the summer as they totally revamped their squad ready for Alonso’s first season in charge.

By far the best performer among their summer recruits has been Morgan Rogers, who has 11 goal contributions in 13 games for the Blues since his £117million arrival from Aston Villa during the World Cup.

Even though they failed to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco on deadline day, they did make other recruitments that have looked like proving shrewd signings, including Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria, Jordan Henderson and Maxence Lacroix.

It is too early to judge the likes of Danny Welbeck, Emi Martinez and Geovany Quenda. Marco Palestra has been disappointing so far.

It has been a reasonable but not spectacular start to life at Chelsea for Alonso. There have been some decent wins under the Spaniard but also some poor defending and a few performances where it was difficult to detect his tactical influence.

Arteta keeps Arsenal stars hungry as rest of season predicted

Alex Scott told to reject £100m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal handed boost

He has kept his cards close to his chest when speaking to the media but this has felt at times to be a slight obstacle to him developing the strong relationship with Chelsea fans that he and they no doubt want. So has not playing Estevao more.

His team selections were poor against Spurs and Sunderland. It is still early doors for Alonso, who continues to insist Chelsea will look very difficult by the time the season is drawing to a close in May.

At the beginning of the season I predicted that Chelsea would finish fourth, but I have not seen enough from them yet to convince me they will finish quite that high. We’re talking small margins, though, and over the course of 38 league games I do believe they will be good enough to sneak into the Champions League with a fifth-place finish, providing England can claim one of the extra European slots as it always seems to.

Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer, Moises Caicedo and Rogers staying fit for the bulk of the season is imperative if they are to return to Europe’s premier competition. If those key men do remain available at Alonso’s disposal, they should gradually improve.

#1843. Arsenal starlet sent off after nightmare performance as England U19s routed

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Marli Salmon was sent off as England Under-19s fell to a heavy defeat against Austria.

The 17-year-old made his debut for that age group last week in a comfortable win over Slovenia, having been called up as an injury replacement.

However, it was a much more difficult game for Salmon on Tuesday as his afternoon came to a premature end.

The Arsenal defender got the nod against Austria and it was an eventful start to the match, with three goals inside the opening ten minutes.

Austria scored again before half-time to lead 3-1 and that was still the scoreline heading into the final 20 minutes of the match.

Salmon was booked for dissent, having shouted in the referee’s face and waved his arm angrily after conceding a free-kick.

Four minutes later, the teenager was then shown a straight red card to complete a miserable occasion for him.

Reigan Heskey played a loose pass back that left his team-mates scrambling and Salmon could not cut out the danger on the halfway line.

Austria’s Johannes Moser got to the ball first and was running clean through on goal, only for Salmon to slide in and bring him down.

He immediately punched the ground in frustration and did not even look back at the referee, knowing the red card was coming, and he began trudging off the pitch.

Austria went on to score another goal with the man advantage and secure a 4-1 win.

It is the second international break in a row that an Arsenal player has been sent off for the England U19s.

Max Dowman was shown a straight red card last month against the USA for a reckless challenge.

Salmon was shown a straight red card for dissent while captaining Arsenal’s Under-21s in a 1-0 defeat by Ipswich Town back in Feburary. He signed his first professional deal with the Gunners in April.

#1842. Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Wirtz stars as Klopp’s side hit best form to top group

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:25

Germany thrashed the Netherlands 5-0 on Monday at the Olympiastadion in Berlin in the final round of the Nations League group stage.

In a convincing performance, the four-time world champions produced their best football since the arrival of Jurgen Klopp, who took charge of the national team after the disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.

With goals from Derry Scherhant, Nico Schlotterbeck, Brajan Gruda and Florian Wirtz, who scored twice, the Germans produced an impressive result against opponents who were also fighting for top spot in the group.

The victory took on even greater importance because of the situation before the match. Germany began the round in third place in Group A2, level on points with Greece and behind the Dutch, and risked missing out on the quarter-finals. With the win, they reached 11 points, overtook their rivals on goal difference and finished the first phase at the top, securing a place among the best eight in the competition.

One of the stars of the night was Derry Scherhant. Klopp’s selection on the left of the attack scored his first goal for the senior Germany team.

A native of Berlin, the 24-year-old winger, who plays for Freiburg, took the opportunity to make his mark in front of the crowd of his home city. His exuberant celebration after finding the top corner past Bart Verbruggen reflected the special significance of the moment in his international career.

The goal also rewarded the faith the manager has placed in the attacker. Scherhant was only making his fourth appearance for the national team and has earned his place amid the renewal carried out by Klopp since he took over.

The chance given to the Freiburg player is part of a strategy that seeks to widen the squad’s options, without restricting selections to the best-known names in German football. Against the Netherlands, the youngster delivered and showed that he can be an interesting option in attack.

Another standout was Wirtz, who again showed how his talent can make a difference in a Germany shirt. The attacking midfielder scored twice in the second half and was decisive in turning a lead built before the break into a rout. His ability to find space, accelerate attacks and arrive in positions to shoot gave another dimension to the German attack.

The performance reinforces one of the main positive certainties of the early days of Klopp’s reign: Wirtz is capable of taking on the team’s technical leadership.

As well as the brilliance of the number 17 and Scherhant’s first goal, the match also underlined the importance of the opportunities given to other young players. Gruda, who had already scored in the 3-1 win over Serbia, found the net again during this international break and has now scored two goals for the national team.

Left-back Philipp Treu was also among the starters, benefiting from the opening up of opportunities by the manager. These are names that help to give shape to a project still under construction and show that Klopp intends to increase competition in different positions.

It was a well-played and competitive first half, with good link-up play and quick transitions. At home, Germany had more possession and went for a proactive game, with a high line and patience to find space.

In the 41st minute, they found it: Scherhant received the ball on the right, got past Denzel Dumfries and curled a lovely shot across goal into the top corner past Verbruggen.

The Netherlands, for their part, took to the pitch practically already qualified. In their tactical approach in the first half, the Dutch opted for a more reactive game: either Xavi Hernandez’s team reached dangerous areas through counter-attacks, or they drew in the German press and built from the back, passing the ball patiently.

At the start of the second half, Germany needed only a few minutes to punish the visitors again. Fourteen minutes into the half, Wirtz began a move down the left, tried to play a one-two with Scherhant, but saw Dumfries step in front of him. The Liverpool midfielder then regained the ball, dribbled past the Dutch full-back and struck hard with his left foot from the edge of the area to make it 2-0.

From there it became a stroll. The Netherlands clearly felt the blow, and the hosts took advantage to turn the win into a rout. Schlotterbeck, with a header, Wirtz, with another stunning goal, and Gruda gave the match its final numbers.

#1840. How Nigeria can qualify for AFCON 2027 after Tanzania draw

Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for next summer’s Africa Cup of Nations have taken a further hit, after a disappointing goalless draw with Tanzania.

The Super Eagles, who back in the autumn international break were beaten 3-0 by Guinea-Bissau at the Estadio 24 de Setembro, appeared to have got back on track with victory over Tanzania last Friday.

A 3-1 win in Uyo - achieved without Victor Osimhen - coupled with Guinea-Bissau being held to a surprise draw away at Madagascar, was the perfect scenario for Nigeria heading into the reverse fixture at the Amaan Stadium on Tuesday afternoon.

However, Eric Chelle’s surprising decision to start without Alex Iwobi and Ola Aina in Zanzibar ultimately backfired. Despite dominating possession and creating numerous chances, the Super Eagles simply could not find a breakthrough and will look back at the game as two points dropped.

How costly a 0-0 draw against a side ranked 117th in the world actually is will become clearer after Guinea-Bissau face Madagascar, though it is unlikely that Nigeria will get two favours in the space of four days.

Now, while the result moves Nigeria level on points with Guinea-Bissau in their AFCON 2027 qualification group, they have played a game more and it’s important to remember a runners-up spot may not be enough to advance to next summer’s tournament.

This is because Tanzania have already qualified for AFCON 2027 by virtue of being co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda.

#1839. "Magical" - German media rave over Liverpool star Florian Wirtz after 5-0 win vs the Netherlands

By Lewis Blain | 17 Nov 2026 07:18, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 07:24

Germany continued their impressive progress under former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp with a commanding 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday evening, with Florian Wirtz producing a standout performance.

The Reds midfielder scored twice in his 50th international appearance, including a spectacular left-footed effort, as Germany recorded their biggest victory over their neighbours since 1959.

Wirtz's display earned widespread praise in his homeland, with several publications awarding him the highest possible grade on the German school-style marking system, where 1 is the best, and 6 is the worst.

SPORT1 awarded Wirtz 1/6, describing his performance as "Ein magischer Abend des Hoffnungsträgers" - a 'magical' evening from the team's star of hope.

The publication acknowledged that he initially struggled to influence proceedings but praised his response after the interval, highlighting his spectacular first goal, subsequent brace-completing finish and ability to dictate Germany's attacking play. Sport Bild also hailed the Liverpool star's 'magic' on an impressive night.

FOCUS Online and Eurosport Germany also awarded Wirtz 1/6, with the latter describing him as the "überragende Mann" - the 'outstanding' player - after his two goals and impressive work out of possession.

FOCUS were particularly impressed by his response to an imperfect moment, joking that he had once dribbled the ball out of play unchallenged before showing his true quality with a "superb brace".

The Frankfurter Rundschau also handed him 1/6, describing him as the "Dreh- und Angelpunkt im Offensivspiel" - the 'focal point' of Germany's attacking play - while suggesting Klopp's system was allowing him to flourish.

Märkische Oderzeitung were slightly less generous, awarding Wirtz 1.5/6, but still praised his technical quality and two excellent finishes. They noted that he initially struggled to find decisive openings before becoming increasingly influential after the hour mark.

Sportschau did not provide a rating but similarly acknowledged that Wirtz was relatively subdued during the first half, before writing that he "Krönte seinen immer stärkeren Auftritt dann mit zwei Treffern" - capped his 'increasingly influential performance' with two goals.

The German media's enthusiasm inevitably raises the question of whether Wirtz can reproduce his international form more consistently at Anfield heading into a busy festive period.

There is little doubt that the 23-year-old has shown encouraging signs during his second season at Liverpool, registering two goals and five assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. However, these returns are still considerably below the extraordinary numbers he produced during his time at Bayer Leverkusen.

Wirtz registered 35 goals and 44 assists in 140 Bundesliga appearances for Leverkusen, becoming one of Europe's most exciting attacking midfielders. While adapting to English football and the Reds' demands takes time, he has yet to consistently reach those same creative and goalscoring heights for his club.

There have been encouraging developments, including scoring and assisting in their 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on November 8th, but the German's international performances are increasingly setting the benchmark for what supporters will expect.

His next opportunity to demonstrate that improvement comes in a huge Premier League encounter, with Liverpool welcoming Manchester United to Anfield on Sunday 22nd November.

After producing two goals against the Netherlands and earning a near-unanimous collection of top marks in Germany, Wirtz will return to Merseyside with considerable confidence. Klopp's influence on the national team has also provided an encouraging reminder of the football that Wirtz can produce when operating with freedom and confidence.

Liverpool will hope that his international brilliance can become a more regular feature at club level, particularly with one of their biggest fixtures of the season approaching.

#1838. Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide while at Manchester United

Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated suicide while playing at Manchester United.

The ex-England striker, who remains United’s record goalscorer, has spoken publicly of his struggles with mental health and alcohol consumption in the past.

But he has now revealed in a candid interview that at his ‘lowest point’ he spent days at home drinking and considered taking his own life.

Speaking on the ‘Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan’ podcast, Rooney explained: “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.”

“Then I didn’t want (his eldest son) Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.

“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to be see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.

“I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, (I) really struggled with it.”

Kai Rooney, the eldest of Wayne’s four children, is now 17 years old and impressing in United’s academy ranks.

Asked to remember the lowest point of his life, Rooney continued: "When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink. This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise."

He added that he “struggled to deal with it all” and acknowledged he “needed help to get through it” after a conversation with his wife Coleen.

The heyday of Rooney’s playing career saw him lift a wealth of domestic and European titles with United. It was during that time, though, that he revealed tried to “mask” his struggles with mental health to avoid “showing weakness.”

“Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that.

“I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married.

“It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't.

“It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.

“Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it.”

#1837. Prediction: Manchester City vs Fulham

Desperately seeking a domestic response this weekend, Manchester City will welcome Fulham to the Etihad on Saturday lunchtime.

With the rest of England’s elite making their respective returns from November’s international break, there are plenty of attractive Premier League betting promotions available.

Ahead of Saturday’s showdown from the Etihad, you can find all of the key Manchester City vs Fulham H2H stats here.

Starting with the hosts, while Manchester City might have enjoyed a sensational start to life under Enzo Maresca, the Sky Blues had certainly come crashing back down to earth prior to November’s international break. Last seen putting in another concerning display as they slumped to a deserved 3-1 defeat away at Nottingham Forest, the former Premier League champions now find themselves sat five points adrift of Arsenal and suddenly have an almighty uphill battle on their hands. In fact, watching a record-breaking Brighton leapfrog them into silver medal position, Man City have astonishingly lost each of their previous three consecutive Premier League appearances. Likewise, despite getting November underway with a rollercoaster 3-2 Champions League victory away at RB Leipzig, Maresca’s men are desperately seeking some kind of defensive grit. In fact, Saturday’s hosts have failed to muster a single clean sheet from any of their previous eight straight matchups across all competitions.

Sustaining a knee injury last month, Manchester City will once again be without former Bournemouth star Antoine Semenyo. However, aside from the Ghanian international, Maresca’s camp have reported a clean bill of health ahead of Saturday’s return.

Bagging nine goals in his 10 Premier League appearances so far this season, Norwegian icon Erling Haaland will spearhead Man City’s attack at the Etihad. Both completing their own respective record-breaking moves to Manchester over the summer, Enzo Fernandez should be partnered alongside Elliot Anderson in the middle of the park.

As for the visitors, while Alvaro Arbeloa might still find some pressure on his shoulders in west London, Fulham certainly showed some real signs of life prior to November’s international break. Playing out consecutive 1-1 stalemates against Aston Villa and Newcastle prior to the fortnight interval, the former Real Madrid boss has seen his resurgent squad drag themselves out of the drop zone. In fact, Saturday’s guests are unbeaten in each of their previous four straight Premier League appearances and are enjoying what has become by far their most fruitful spell since Arbeloa’s arrival at Craven Cottage. However, more than aware that they face a monumental challenge this weekend, Fulham hold a nightmare record against the Sky Blues. Including a routine 3-0 defeat when they last travelled to the blue half of Manchester back in February, they have remarkably lost each of their previous 20 straight meetings against the former Premier League champions across all competitions.

While club captain Tom Cairney might have missed out against Newcastle prior to November’s international break after feeling some discomfort in his knee, the 35-year-old could return to Fulham’s squad here. Coming off the bench and bagging a maiden strike of the season last time out, Brazilian striker Rodrigo Muniz could be handed a full recall.

Despite recent speculation over a potential January move away from west London, Nigerian international Calvin Bassey will start at the heart of Fulham’s defence. Completing a big-money move to Craven Cottage over the summer, ex-Southampton youngster Shea Charles will start in the middle of the park.

Remarkably losing each of their final three straight Premier League appearances prior to November’s fortnight interval, Manchester City suddenly have a huge amount of pressure on their shoulders here. Sat five points adrift of defending champions Arsenal, Maresca’s men can’t afford another public slip-up on Saturday lunchtime. However, cruising their way to a stunning 3-0 victory when they last welcomed Fulham to the Etihad back in February, they have remarkably won all of their previous 20 straight showdowns against the Cottagers across all competitions.

#1834. Man United transfer news: Former defender backs move for Chelsea star Estevao

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 08:02

Mikael Silvestre sees Estevao as a player capable of strengthening Manchester United, but does not believe the Red Devils will pursue the forward at this time.

The former France defender, who played for the Old Trafford club between 1999 and 2008, praised the Brazilian’s performance and considered him an interesting option if he were available on the market. However, that prospect hinges on the young player’s willingness to fight for his place at Stamford Bridge.

Silvestre’s assessment comes at a time of significant change at Manchester United. The club invested more than £144m (€170m) in signings last summer and showed an intention to back Michael Carrick after the team finished last season in third place in the Premier League. The start of the new campaign, however, has fallen short of expectations.

The enthusiasm that had arisen among the fans was quickly replaced by dissatisfaction with the results. After the 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea, Manchester United reached nine consecutive matches without a win in all competitions. Neither the reaction against Roma, with a comeback in the Europa League, nor the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford was enough to prevent the departure of Carrick, who was sacked last Thursday (12 November).

Mauricio Pochettino has been chosen to take charge of the team. The Argentinian has officially left the United States national team and is expected to begin work at Manchester United this week, while the board is already focusing its attention on the January transfer window.

Among the possibilities to strengthen the squad, Estevao appears as a name that appeals to Silvestre. The 19-year-old Brazilian is still seeking greater playing time at Chelsea, but he had a standout performance precisely against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge.

In an interview with Betarades.gr, the former player highlighted the forward’s display and pointed to his determination as an obstacle to a possible transfer.

‘Estevao played for Chelsea against Manchester United, and I think he showed why he deserves more playing time. It looks like he is going to fight for his place, so I do not think Manchester United will make a move for him’ - Silvestre said.

The Frenchman’s interpretation is that the Brazilian intends to seize opportunities to establish himself at Chelsea rather than seek a move at this time. Even so, Silvestre left no doubt about his individual assessment of the player.

‘But he is definitely a good player. He plays for the Brazil national team, and I like his style of play. If he were available for transfer, he would be a good signing for Manchester United’ - he added.

Manchester United are set to return to the transfer market in January with the intention of improving the team’s performance in the second half of the season. One of their priorities is signing a left-back, a position for which the club unsuccessfully attempted to sign Lewis Hall from Newcastle in the summer.

The attacking department may also receive attention from the board. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, considered important players for the team, have had starts to the season below expectations, increasing the need to find alternatives in attack.

With Pochettino about to begin his tenure, planning for the next transfer window is gaining importance. Estevao, despite having Silvestre’s approval, would depend on a change of scenery at Chelsea to effectively enter Manchester United’s radar.

For now, the most likely scenario is that the Brazilian will remain in London trying to gain more playing time and consolidate his position at Chelsea.

#1831. Prediction: Newcastle vs Arsenal

Competition: Premier League Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Kickoff: 17:30 GMT Venue: St. James’ Park, Newcastle.

Verdict: Under 2.5 goals Best odds: 123/100 Bookmaker: 1xBet

Arsenal resumes its title defense with a trip to Newcastle on Saturday, carrying a defensive record that gives Mikel Arteta every reason to approach another demanding away fixture with confidence. The champion has collected 27 points and seven clean sheets from its opening ten Premier League matches.

Newcastle has found consistency much harder to come by, although recent results suggest this could become a patient contest with relatively few goals.

Newcastle came close to entering the international break with a useful away victory. Jacob Murphy broke the deadlock at Fulham in the 80th minute, only for Rodrigo Muniz to equalize three minutes later. Harvey Barnes had also passed up a good opportunity, leaving Matthias Jaissle with some encouragement from the performance and frustration over the points that slipped away.

That 1-1 draw followed a 2-0 league victory at Crystal Palace and a 1-0 home defeat against Everton. Each of those three matches finished below the 2.5-goal line, with Newcastle producing enough to remain competitive without consistently finding the finishing touch to settle games.

Against Arsenal, the balance between pressing and protecting midfield will matter. Newcastle’s best route appears to involve choosing its moments to attack, getting Barnes into space and making set pieces count. Giving the visitor repeated opportunities to attack an exposed back line would make an already difficult assignment considerably harder.

Joelinton remains an injury concern after missing the Fulham match, while goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen is unavailable with a hamstring problem. Jacob Ramsey’s one-match suspension applied to the Fulham fixture, leaving him eligible to return against Arsenal.

Arsenal has developed a useful habit of making a single goal sufficient. Its two most recent Premier League outings brought 1-0 victories over Liverpool and Hull City, with Martin Odegaard providing the breakthrough against Hull in the 72nd minute. That performance required patience, particularly while the visiting defense continued to frustrate Arsenal’s attempts to create clear chances.

The broader pattern strengthens the case for another restrained scoreline. Arsenal’s last four league victories have been achieved without conceding, beating Nottingham Forest, Everton, Liverpool and Hull while scoring five goals across those matches. Arteta’s side has been able to protect narrow advantages exceptionally well.

For this trip, another controlled performance looks a reasonable expectation. Newcastle should provide a sterner physical examination than Hull, but Arsenal has already demonstrated at Anfield that it can leave a difficult ground with a clean sheet and three points.

Bukayo Saka remains sidelined, while Max Dowman is suspended. Martin Zubimendi needs assessment after suffering a muscle problem on international duty with Spain.

William Saliba has taken another step toward returning by playing 45 minutes for the under-21 side. His involvement here remains a selection decision, rather than a confirmed return to the starting lineup.

Arsenal deserves favoritism, with its defensive discipline offering the strongest argument for another away victory. Newcastle should make the visitor work for opportunities, however, and the recent scoring patterns suggest this could remain close well into the second half.

Under 2.5 goals is the preferred selection. A 1-0 Arsenal victory is the predicted score, although a tight draw would also fit the reasoning behind the goals bet.

The left-back then signed a new deal with Newcastle until the summer of 2031.

Signing Hall off the back of a new deal at Newcastle will be far from straightforward, but Man United must push to bring the Englishman to Old Trafford next year.

Estevao declined to comment when asked whether his lack of playing time might push him to leave Chelsea in January.

#1827. Arsenal legend and double winner Peter Storey dies aged 81

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Tributes are pouring in for Arsenal legend Peter Storey, who has passed away at the age of 81.

The Surrey-born midfielder, who retired with 19 England caps, first joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and went on to play a vital role in the side which won a league and FA Cup double in 1971.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy. He also lifted the Fairs Cup with the club.

Initially a full-back, he was later moved into midfield, where he spent the remainder of his career and gained a reputation as a crunching tackler.

Storey made 501 appearances in total for Arsenal and is their eighth all-time highest appearance maker. He left north London in 1977 to sign with Fulham before retiring in 1978.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund, which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double Winner, Peter Storey.

“All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.”

Storey’s family added in a statement: "We are deeply saddened by the loss of Peter, a much-loved father and grandfather. He is survived by his three sons and grandchildren, who will miss him dearly. We are deeply grateful for the many kind messages, tributes and good wishes we have received.

“It has been a great comfort to see the affection and respect in which he was held by so many, both within the football community and beyond."

England also paid tribute on their official X account, adding: “We are saddened to learn that Peter Storey – who won 19 caps for the Three Lions in the 1970s – has passed away at the age of 81.

“Our condolences are with Peter’s family and friends at this time.”

Storey hung up his boots when his Fulham contract was cancelled, just eight months after he had signed. He went on to own a north London pub.

He was convicted of a number of criminal offences after retiring from football, including smuggling pornography, keeping a brothel, and financing the production of counterfeit coins, as detailed in his 2010 autobiography ‘True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man’.

Barcelona will reportedly not make a move for Tottenham Hotspur defender Pedro Porro during the January transfer window, but a switch to Camp Nou next summer is a possibility.

Porro, 27, has had his issues at Tottenham, but the right-back was outstanding for Spain at the 2026 World Cup and is an important player for the national side.

There has recently been speculation surrounding Porro's future, with Barcelona planning to be active during the January market due to their defensive issues.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sweden boss Graham Potter was quick to defend Dejan Kulusevski after the forward’s form in this international break was criticised.

Tottenham forward Kulusevski only recently returned from an extended injury layoff. In May 2025, he suffered a complex patella injury and endured a lengthy recovery pockmarked with various setbacks and multiple surgical procedures.

The 26-year-old made a long-awaited comeback earlier this autumn, though, and has now made four cameo appearances for Tottenham.

Those showings were enough to earn him a recall to Potter’s Sweden squad for the November international break, where he has enjoyed substitute appearances totalling 56 minutes in a victory over Bosnia & Herzegovina and a draw with Poland, his first appearances for his nation since November 2024.

His performances this month, though, have been criticised by some in the Swedish press. The outlet TVmatchen dubbed his performance against Bosnia “miserable”, adding: “For obvious reasons not in absolute match form, but looked slow and was never in the game. Was he really ready for this already?”

The news site Svenskafans then described him as “eager” but “rusty”.

Potter, though, has leapt to Kulusevski’s defence, slamming what he considers unwarranted criticism.

“I think the criticism is completely unfair, to be honest,” he told Viaplay following Tuesday’s draw with Poland.

He continued, explaining why he felt Kulusevski was ready to return to the Blagult fold: “He has trained very, very well. You have to judge someone based on a match like that, like it was against Bosnia. It wasn't easy for the substitutes to come into that match.

“Now he just needs to get playing time, and that's completely normal. It's completely normal for anyone who's been out with an injury and is now getting back into match form.”

Kulusevski has yet to score or assist since returning to first-team action, but is only expected to increase his involvement for club and country as he builds back his fitness in the coming weeks.

Speaking last week, Potter acknowledged the need to be gentle with Kulusevski, and he worked with Tottenham to ensure he was not overexerted during the November break.

Michael Carrick has released his first public statement on his Manchester United sacking, calling the job an 'immense privilege' in a classy 411-word tribute to the club's supporters.

The statement, released a little over 24 hours after his dismissal was confirmed, read: 'Dear United Fans, I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

'There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

'With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It's different to anywhere else.

'Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

'It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day. I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

Michael Carrick has broken his silence on his sacking by Manchester United

'We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

'I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

'That means more than a win or two. That's what makes you who you are. That's why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

'A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn't have asked for any more. I'm incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.

'To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

'And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we've shared. I wish you all the very best for what's ahead.

'I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it.

'I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on. Michael.'

The statement follows his former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that Carrick had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of the United legend.

Carrick was left in the lurch by the club's hierarchy - but continued to attend training on Tuesday and Wednesday – amid widespread reports that he would imminently be relieved of his duties.

The classy statement follows Carrick former team-mate Gary Neville suggesting that he had grounds to sue United for their 'disgusting' treatment of his dismissal

Neville told Sky Sports News: 'In the last 24-48 hours it's been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who's a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino.

'It's just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you'd be getting sued.

'The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it's just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership.

'I don't think anybody comes out of this well at all.'

Less than an hour prior to Carrick's statement United confirmed his replacement, Pochettino, will take the reins after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

The 54-year-old Argentine will take charge of the US’s CONCACAF Nations League double-header against Haiti in Miami on Saturday and Cincinnati on Wednesday before beginning his new job as United boss on Wednesday.

His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

Pochettino is due to give a pre-match press conference at 2.15pm on Friday but is not expected to speak about United until he arrives next week due to his remaining contracted to US Soccer.

United have agreed to pay more than £10million to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation

A statement from the club read: ‘Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

‘The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team.

‘The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

‘Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

‘During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular UEFA Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

‘In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023. Most recently he led the U.S. Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.’

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A)

#1818. Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Jurgen Klopp sends clear message that spells trouble for Nations League rivals

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 09:46

Jurgen Klopp is in dreamland after witnessing a “truly extraordinary” performance from his Germany side in a statement 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.

The four-time world champions began the night sitting third in League A Group 2 and knew that they had to claim maximum points against the Oranje at the summit to secure top spot and qualify for the quarter-finals.

With so much at stake heading into the sixth and final matchday, Die Mannschaft rose to the occasion in prolific fashion, claiming their biggest win against their Dutch neighbours since 1959 when they won 7-0.

Derry Scherhant opened the scoring just before half time with a sensational maiden international goal, setting the tone for a dominant second-half display.

Overwhelmed by Germany’s relentless high press, the Netherlands had no answer as two goals from Florian Wirtz, and strikes from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda, sealed a statement triumph for Klopp’s side.

“What we’ve just witnessed was truly extraordinary,” the former Liverpool manager told reporters post-match. “The game was extraordinary, and incredibly difficult.”

“Against a really good opponent, you have to find a way to win. We had to adapt and make a few adjustments, some fairly significant ones, but we made them. We took away a lot of their strengths, and then we scored some incredible goals. That was unbelievable.

“It was a fantastic football match and a wonderful experience. I wouldn’t have ever dreamed of having the chance to do this in Berlin in front of a sold-out crowd. In the final international game of the year, it’s amazing.”

In addition to progressing to the quarter-finals, the result served as compelling evidence of Germany's renaissance and progress under Klopp, with his arrival fostering renewed optimism around his youthful squad.

Germany failed to win their opening two Nations League matches, but they ended their group campaign with 11 points (W3 D2 L1) and have conceded a competition-low three goals in six games.

"The moment I arrived here, I fell in love with this team at first sight,” said Klopp. “I'm at the beginning of this journey.

“I simply feel that we have a fantastic football team and a very good footballing idea that can work extremely well. If we can get these highly-talented players firing, then we're going to be a very difficult team to play against.

“We scored some incredible goals and, with increasing confidence, put in a great performance in front of a fantastic crowd. It’s been a lot of fun to work with this team, and we feel like we have a very special group of players here.

“But this is still only just the beginning – after six games, we can’t say that we’ve arrived where we want to be yet, as there are still lots of things we can improve on.”

"Everyone who was here today is going home with a smile, and won't be questioning the German national team for the next three or four months. That's a good thing," Klopp added when referring to the negativity that lingered previously around the national team.

Looking ahead to the quarter-final draw on Friday, Klopp added: "The lads can head home now with a smile on their faces as the group winners. We’ll watch the draw later this week and wait and see what sort of crunch match we’ll get, as there are only strong teams left.”

Germany, who have risen to 11th in the FIFA World Rankings, will play their two-legged quarter-final tie in March 2027, with a first-placed finish in League A rewarded with a second leg on home soil.

#1817. Who will England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed after Spain win

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

He is the only player in Seattle history to record multiple seasons with 15+ assists, with Nicolas Lodieiro the only other Sounders player to do so even once, back in 2018.

Sergi Solans tallied 15 regular-season goals, becoming the fifth player in Real Salt Lake history to score at least 15 in a single season.

His total is the second highest by a player in his first season with the club, behind only Jeff Cunningham's 16 goals in 2006.

Only Chicago Fire against D.C. United and Sporting Kansas City against Colorado Rapids have longer active unbeaten runs in the postseason (seven each).

The Sounders have won 21 of their 29 home playoff matches (D3 L5), and the 21 home wins rank third in MLS Cup Playoffs history behind LA Galaxy (38) and Columbus Crew (22).

Since the beginning of 2014, Seattle have lost just once in 22 home playoff games (1-0 to LAFC in 2022, W18 D3).

#1813. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the eight teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position was Group A4 was confirmed after their win over Wales on Tuesday night, though it is Norway joining them in the knockout phases following a remarkable comeback win against Denmark.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, Portugal

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, Norway

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

#1812. New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino reacts to ‘city is blue’ comment with six-word promise

Mauricio Pochettino has said to “give him time” to make Manchester United the dominant club in the city again as he prepares to start work.

Pochettino will take charge of Man United for the first time against Liverpool on Sunday after being appointed to succeed Michael Carrick, who was sacked last week with the club sitting 18th in the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s return to club management has been delayed after being allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States national team.

His last game ended in a 2-0 win for USA against Haiti in Cincinnati during the early hours on Wednesday (UK time) to wrap up an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

AC Milan forward Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a spectacular overhead kick and teenager Julian Hall doubled the hosts’ lead before half-time.

After bidding an emotional farewell to the USA supporters inside the stadium, Pochettino immediately turned his attentions to the task at hand with Man United and the rivalry with Manchester City.

Told by former Man City loanee DaMarcus Beasley that “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue” in the TNT Sports US studio after the game, Pochettino responded: “You will see. Give me time.

“The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenalin you want to feel.

“We need to add our common sense… we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing.”

Pochettino heads to Old Trafford tasked with steering Man United out of the relegation zone before he can target winning titles and eventually usurping Man City as the dominant team in the city.

United have not been crowned Premier League champions since Sir Alex Ferguson retired, with the legendary Scotsman final season being the last time the club finished above their neighbours in the table.

Additional reporting by Press Association.

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 10:28

Arsenal have been interested in the profile of Eli Junior Kroupi for many months, and the forward should be one of the talking points of the next January transfer window. The London club have everything to be the ideal destination for the young France international.

Author of a very good 2025-26 season with Bournemouth in his first year in the Premier League, Kroupi scored 13 goals in 33 league matches. The 20-year-old striker was a revelation and quickly appeared on the radar of Europe’s biggest clubs.

‘Last summer, a fifth metatarsal injury compromised a possible departure, which the player was considering,’ - RMC Sport reported. The French outlet says the former Lorient player will be one of the attractions of the next summer transfer window, as he still interests heavyweights.

Kroupi has only just returned from his injury, however. He has played just four cameos with Bournemouth, but he reminded everyone of the extent of his talent with France. The 20-year-old won his first two caps and scored his first goal for France against Turkey (2-1).

During that international gathering, the forward made an impression and is considered one of the positives. He is highly rated by Zinedine Zidane’s staff, RMC Sport points out. His status is therefore potentially already changing, and that is before his expected transfer next summer.

For this important next step in his career, Arsenal have everything to be the ideal destination. While PSG, Barcelona and Bayern Munich are also interested in his profile, Arsenal have been trying to sign him for many months. Mikel Arteta is described as a fan of the new France international by TalkSport.

A move to the London club would allow Kroupi to stay in the Premier League. It is the biggest league in the world and he has already found his feet there with his 13 goals in his first season. Arsenal also appear to be still looking for a number nine, with Kroupi seen as their ‘ideal candidate’.

Viktor Gyokeres has failed to establish himself at the London club.

A departure is already being talked about for the next January transfer window. Kroupi’s profile is also compatible with Arteta’s style of play, as the Frenchman is a quick, technical striker with a great eye for goal.

Joining Arsenal would allow Kroupi to take an important step in his career by joining a top club. The English side are back among Europe’s best teams after their Premier League title win and Champions League final last year. It is one of the most attractive projects, along with that of PSG, at the moment.

However, in Paris, competition is strong at the tip of the attack with 2025 Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembele, who is set to extend his contract. The problem is the same at Bayern Munich with their 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who has also signed a new deal.

In London, Kai Havertz, who can notably be repositioned behind the centre-forward, represents less and more accessible competition for Kroupi.

#1809. How Manchester United could line up in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game vs Liverpool as big calls made

The Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United is officially underway, and his first game is just days away.

The Red Devils return from the final international break of 2026 to face the daunting prospect of visiting arch-rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend.

Pochettino inherits a side with just one win in 10 top-flight games this term, a string of results that have left Man Utd in the relegation zone.

The Argentine’s style of play centres around a high-press and an ability to build from the back - two things United have struggled with so far this season.

Injuries across the pitch will impact Pochettino’s selection, with Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko definitely ruled out for the trip to Anfield.

In goal, Senne Lammens is established first-choice and that is unlikely to change with Pochettino’s arrival, while the Argentine might be tempted to copy Michael Carrick and play Leny Yoro at right-back, instructing the Frenchman to tuck in and form a three-man defence in possession.

However, Diogo Dalot will likely start at right-back, with a much more simple defensive approach.

Yoro could therefore partner Ayden Heaven in the heart of defence to give United a bit more pace than a backline featuring Harry Maguire, but the experience of Lisandro Martinez may be hard to ignore as Pochettino balances a squad lacking in confidence.

Patrick Dorgu is a doubt after being sent home from international duty with Denmark, but is said to be winning his battle to be fit for the Anfield trip and could replicate what Antonee Robinson did for Pochettino at left-back.

With the USA, Pochettino had settled on a 4-3-3 formation, with the midfield featuring a sitting player behind two more proactive team-mates.

Pochettino’s immediate issue with the Man United squad will be the fact that there is no clear candidate as a holding midfielder. The injured Baleba does well at screening the backline, but his strengths rely on driving forward with the ball.

#1807. Who makes up Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff at Manchester United?

Manchester United have turned to Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager, and a new backroom staff will be joining him for his return to the Premier League.

After identifying ex-Tottenham boss Pochettino as the desired replacement for sacked head coach Michael Carrick, Man Utd quickly agreed personal terms - before approaching the USA to extract their target from a four-year contract only signed following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

It has been reported that the total compensation package United will have to pay the US Soccer Federation could be north of £10million, once fees for Pochettino’s staff have been included.

Assistant manager Jesus Perez has worked with Pochettino since his first job in management, employed initially as an analyst at Espanyol in LaLiga.

After building a strong relationship with Pochettino, Spaniard Perez was promoted to No2 when the Argentine was appointed manager of Southampton in 2013, and has been his assistant at every job since.

Perez and Pochettino joked about the United job during the World Cup, with the former apparently very keen on working at Old Trafford.

There are four other members of staff likely to make the move across the Atlantic.

Miguel D’Agostino is a former team-mate of Pochettino’s, with the duo having played together at Newell’s Old Boys in their native Argentina.

Initially working as a scout for Pochettino at Espanyol, D’Agostino has also followed his compatriot from club to club since then.

Toni Jimenez is another to have worked with Pochettino at every club he has managed so far, plus the US national team. A goalkeeping coach, Jimenez first linked up with Pochettino in 2011 at Espanyol.

The penultimate member of coaching staff mentioned in reports has not been involved in Pochettino’s setup as long as the others, but has a very close relationship to the former Chelsea manager.

Sebastiano Pochettino is Mauricio’s son and started working within his father’s coaching team at Spurs. He has continued in his role as a sports scientist.

Silvia Tuya - full name Silvia Tuya Vinas - is a strength and conditioning coach, currently employed by the USMNT.

Tuya will become the first female coach of the men’s first team squad at Old Trafford, creating history ahead of a new chapter for Manchester United.

The strength and conditioning coach will be familiar with creating such history, having previously become the first female coach in the history of the USMNT’s senior squad when she joined the backroom staff in October 2024.

#1806. Mauricio Pochettino urges Pep Guardiola to take USA job after revealing talks that sparked Man United U-turn

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 11:04

Outgoing USA manager Mauricio Pochettino has publicly advised Pep Guardiola to pursue the vacant national team job as he prepares to begin his new role at Manchester United.

The 54-year-old Argentine will bid an emotional farewell to the Stars and Stripes when he takes charge of his final fixture against Haiti on Tuesday before officially taking over from Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

With the US Soccer Federation now searching for a successor, former Manchester City boss Guardiola has emerged as a ‘top target’ for the vacant managerial role.

Addressing the media during his final pre-match press conference, Pochettino gave his endorsement to the legendary Catalan coach - who won 20 trophies across 10 seasons at Man City - and urged him to accept an offer if approached.

"Take it," Pochettino told reporters. "Why? Because it’s a perfect moment to arrive at the federation.

“Everything is on the right path, in the right direction. Of course, take it. Of course, you are going to find really good players, good people – the players can fit his style."

While Pochettino is backing Guardiola for international management, a previous conversation between the pair helped trigger the Argentine's own return to the club game.

Last week, Man United confirmed Pochettino as their new head coach after dismissing Carrick, who has left the Red Devils languishing in the Premier League relegation zone following a dismal start to the campaign.

Taking the reins at Carrington marks Pochettino's first club appointment since departing Chelsea at the conclusion of the 2023-24 season, adding to previous English top-flight stints with Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur.

Pochettino was given the green light by Man United to see out his USA commitments first, with his final outing against Haiti largely a formality after the Stars and Stripes secured a dominant 6-0 win in the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday.

In an interview with The Telegraph ahead of his departure, Pochettino disclosed that he confessed to Guardiola how much he longed for the daily routine of club football when the pair met at an MLS game between New York Red Bulls and New York City FC in September.

“I am ready [to return],” Pochettino explained. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything… this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

Pochettino’s candid remarks about craving a Premier League comeback may frustrate some USA supporters, given that he had put pen to paper on a new four-year contract extension just one month before his discussion with Guardiola.
