#1805. 'I was one day away from falling into a coma': JAKE O'BRIEN, the Premier League's only diabetic player, on his brush with death, managing his condition in the dressing room - and why he was 'never close' to leaving Everton last summer

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 13 November 2026

There are few sights more incendiary to the modern manager than a footballer reaching for his phone as soon as he walks through the dressing room door. So you can imagine the reaction Jake O’Brien received when he pulled out his mobile just before one half-time team talk.

But the Everton and Republic of Ireland defender had a good excuse: he’s the only Type One diabetic playing in the Premier League.

O’Brien’s body is unable to create insulin, the hormone that regulates the amount of glucose in your blood.

Loaded on his mobile is an app linked via Bluetooth to a circular device on his arm which gives a reading of his blood sugar levels. It is then that he takes out a needle and injects the necessary insulin dose into his thigh or stomach.

‘There was one guy who didn’t react too well. Mentioning no names! He was saying: "What are you doing on your phone?"' O’Brien recalls. ‘But he soon realised what it was for.’

It can also come as a shock to the uninitiated among his team-mates.

‘One or two are taken aback at first,’ he says. ‘It can be a bit confusing. “What’s he doing?’’ Or maybe those that are a little squeamish, but they soon get used to it. It's only a small needle.'

Everton and Ireland defender Jake O'Brien is the only diabetic footballer in the Premier League

O'Brien (pictured attending an awareness workshop put on by Everton) revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador

O'Brien (pictured with his partner Sophie) says some of his team-mates are 'taken aback' when he injects himself with insulin (Source: Instagram/Obrienjake_)

Tracking blood glucose levels is now an everyday part of O'Brien's life but it is a life that was unwittingly put in jeopardy prior to his diagnosis at 16.

O’Brien was later told he had been just one day away from slipping into a coma when his concerned parents ushered him to the doctors near the family home in Youghal, County Cork, for a check-up.

Their sports-mad son, who had won national titles at boxing and hurling, was tired, losing weight and had an insatiable thirst despite drinking eight to nine litres of water a day. He had lost seven kilograms in just over a week. A blood test revealed his blood sugar was ten times what was considered stable and he was rushed to hospital.

‘I was told I was a day away from a coma,' says O'Brien. 'If I had gone to sleep that night without having gone to the doctor, who knows?’

He went into hospital that night weighing 53kg, or just over eight stone. Two weeks post-diagnosis he was back up to 60kg, and within two years he had put on a whopping 30kg.

'Yeah, 30kg,' laughs O'Brien. 'I know it's not normal. It must have been some grocery bill for Mum, but I was motivated to put on the weight, going to the gym all the time.

‘I was a bit naive about it all,' he deadpans. ‘I never expected to have anything but once I knew what diabetes was, I didn’t wallow in it, I took it as a positive. Everything just clicked for me physically. I just thought, "Right, now I know what’s wrong, I can get on with my life again".

‘It was a pain going in and out of hospital, but I just took it as education and wanted to get my sport back on track.

'My family are... I wouldn't say cold, but matter of fact. Supportive, obviously, but they are all sporty too, so it was just, "Get on with it".'

O'Brien's life in the Premier League would have seemed inconceivable when he fell down to 53kg as a teenager and was hospitalised

He is now an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with

Today, relaxing in the cafe at Everton’s Finch Farm training complex, O’Brien is an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with.

There’s a Cork-lilt to his softly spoken Irish tone. He’s polite and engaging and it’s clear he revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador, spreading the message that diagnosis doesn’t have to end your dreams.

Such has been his impact, he has even attracted support from fans of the other club in the city.

One, six-year-old Liverpool fan Louis, reached out via Instagram to ask O’Brien how he kept up his glucose levels during a game and whether he suffered any ‘hypos’ - the expression for hypoglycemic episodes, when the blood sugar drops too low and leaves you faint or dizzy.

Louis, whose siblings Paisley and Evie also have Type One diabetes, followed up by challenging O’Brien to a penalty shootout. If the Everton man lost, he faced a forfeit, he would have to shout ‘Up the Reds’ on social media.

‘You play for the wrong team but you're still a Type One hero, and Mum says you're proof that diabetes doesn't stop you from playing at the top level,’ posted Louis.

Touched by the message, O’Brien asked Everton to invite the youngster and his family to training for a kickabout, although ultimately, we are assured they reached a compromise on the penalties forfeit.

‘I’ve struck up a rapport with some kids and groups here and in Ireland,' says O'Brien. 'They often have the same story as mine of not being sure what the future holds.

‘There’s a big misconception about diabetes over what it is and the limitations it brings.

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over.’

‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel. I may inject four times before a night game and a bit more at half-time'

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over,’ says O'Brien, who also excelled at boxing and hurling as a boy (Source: TikTok/Everton)

The centre back credits boxing for helping discipline with his diet but underlines ‘no food is off limits, it’s just about applying common sense'.

A typical day sees him eat eggs, salmon and dates for breakfast to match his insulin doses to the carbohydrates he’s taking on around 9.30am before training. Afterwards he’ll have a light lunch at 2pm then take something back from the training ground for a light evening meal.

‘I just have to watch carbohydrates. I’ll eat more of them on match day but then work out my insulin ratio to the amount I eat and whether I need to inject more.

‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel, I may inject four times before a night game and inject a bit more at half-time. If it’s not quite right you may get a bit heavy-legged or if I get a few cramps I may need a gel. But I've had no dangerous episodes.'

When World Diabetes Day dawns on Saturday, O’Brien will be fully focused on preparing to play for Ireland in Austria in the Nations League.

It will give him a chance to revert to his favoured centre back position having been asked to fill in predominantly at right back under David Moyes.

He acknowledges it's not his preferred role but dismisses rumours that he wanted to leave as a result in the summer.

'There was nothing in that,' O'Brien affirms. ‘I was never close to leaving.

'People know I'm not a natural right back but I'll play wherever I need to, to help the team. We're only a small squad so it’s important everyone chips in.

‘There’s a lot of different right backs. I see Arsenal have centre backs playing at right back so I can take pointers from them but then again, I am 6ft 6in so I’m not the average shape.’

O'Brien insists there was 'nothing in' reports that he wanted to leave Everton last summer to get more minutes at his preferred position of centre back

At least O’Brien has former Everton captain Seamus Coleman on hand for advice.

‘Seamus is a good friend. He still gives me pointers of where to be, positioning wise and seeing the game differently.'

Ireland assistant John O'Shea, a versatile defender himself in his Manchester United days, is another mentor. O’Shea and Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrímsson were at Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch O'Brien play his part in Everton's recent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

'Heimir is a good guy,' says O'Brien. 'Very understanding. It's always a nice change of scenery to link up with Ireland. We've got a difficult couple of games (Austria and Kosovo) but hopefully if we get two wins it’s within reach.'

Indeed, if there's a mantra that personifies O'Brien's outlook on life, no matter what knocks you take, it is: always believe you can still achieve.

'Don’t be afraid and don’t let anything hold you back, that's what I say.'

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, though, everyone would be glad that the decision was made to sign the young Italian. To say he’s exploded this season would be an understatement and he’s perhaps the biggest gem at the club right now.

#1801. Exclusive: Charlton boss Nathan Jones among managers objecting to FA rule change

Charlton manager Nathan Jones is among a number of head coaches in English football’s top four divisions to have objected to the reduction in how many yellow cards leads to a touchline ban.

Standard Sport understands that at a recent managers’ meeting, Jones and other head coaches from clubs among the 92 argued a 2023 change in FA rules towards stricter punishments for technical-area misconduct remains unjustified at a time when football managers have never faced greater pressure and volatility.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is incongruous with an increasingly demanding working environment.

Head coaches across the Premier League and EFL are understood to have this season been shown research that suggests managers’ behaviour usually improves once they reach three bookings.

Managers are regularly reminded of a variety of regulations including technical-area misconduct rules during meetings with the FA’s disciplinary teams, who often present research and statistics to contextualise changes to rules or emerging trends.

Ahead of the 2018-19 season, new rules were introduced to clean up touchline behaviour. Managers across the FA Cup, EFL, Carabao Cup, EFL Trophy and National League could receive yellow and red cards for the first time, with four yellows resulting in a one-match touchline ban.

It is the view of some managers, including Jones, that the FA’s move to bring forward touchline bans from four yellow cards to three is unreasonable

Premier League managers would receive only verbal cautions for “irresponsible behaviour” but then the top flight fell in line with the same level of punishment from 2019-20 onwards.

A further update was made ahead of the 2023-24 campaign when the FA launched a new ‘Participant Behaviour Charter’ as part of its ‘Love Football, Protect the Game’ campaign, developed alongside the Premier League, EFL, Women's Super League, Women's Championship, National League System (Steps 1–4), and PGMOL (now Pro Ref), with input from the League Managers Association (LMA) and Professional Footballers' Association (PFA).

The charter’s aim was to improve the image of the game and maintain a positive environment. Four yellows for a managerial suspension was reduced to three and has remained so ever since.

A new cut-off for technical-area cautions was introduced this season. Managers who receive their third technical-area booking after the 37th round of EFL league matches do not incur an immediate suspension. At that point an automatic one-match touchline ban is triggered only if a fourth yellow card is picked up in a subsequent game.

Compared with its peak, the number of technical-area cautions issued has decreased by 17 per cent since the introduction of the ‘Participation Behaviour Charter’, FA sources say.

Under the FA’s ‘Laws of the Game’, other staff and substitutes in a technical area can also be cautioned or even sent off.

In certain circumstances, managers and head coaches can get booked or sent off on behalf of the misconduct of others in their technical area if the fourth official reports a situation deserving of punishment to the referee but cannot verify who in the technical area committed the offence. In such situations, FA rules state cards can be shown to the “manager or most senior coach in [the technical] area”.

#1800. England centre-backs under 21: Five options Thomas Tuchel may need for Three Lions future

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 11:27

While England were raking in the plaudits for the manner of their epic 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, it became evident over the November international break that Thomas Tuchel could soon run into issues.

Not only did Tuchel use Jarell Quansah - generally viewed as a right-back for the national team - as a central defender against the world champions, the height of 34-year-old Dan Burn was preferred to Jarrad Branthwaite on the substitutes' bench.

Furthermore, Josh Acheampong's withdrawal from the England Under-21 squad left Lee Carsley without a single centre-back who was earning regular Premier League football at this stage of their career.

Tuchel is not necessarily short of centre-back options. As well as Branthwaite, Bournemouth's James Hill earned his first senior call-up, and the likes of Marc Guehi, John Stones, Trevoh Chalobah and Levi Colwill - all at various stages of their career - will contribute for England going forward.

Nevertheless, there are a glaring lack of realistic options at Under-21 level and below, and it may lead to certain players being fast-tracked up the pecking order and into Three Lions contention.

Here, Sports Mole suggests five defenders who are under 21 that have the potential to become a permanent member of the England squad in the future.

With 55 appearances for Chelsea prior to his 21st birthday, Acheampong is the standout defensive option for the Under-21s. It is arguably a surprise that he is yet to be called up to the senior squad.

The Blues academy graduate has been used as the right-sided option of a back three or as a right-back by Xabi Alonso, starting nine times in 2026-27 across all competitions.

At this stage of his career, the assumption is that he will transition into a centre-back on a permanent basis, and there is the potential for him to rival Quansah for his position in the squad going forward.

For the reasons highlighted, Acheampong will be viewed as a key member of the Under-21s squad prior to next summer's European Championship.

When Coventry City signed 18-year-old Stephen Mfuni on loan from Manchester City, it felt an unusual decision. Would a teenager with minimal senior experience be used by a newly-promoted club who are expected to be scrapping for Premier League survival?

However, not only has Mfuni made three starts and two substitute outings in the top flight, he completed the 90 minutes in victories over Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, as well as netting in the 4-1 demolition of Newcastle United.

Frank Lampard has already been raving about the potential of Mfuni, who also made eight starts for Watford in last season's Championship.

Of all the English centre-backs below the age of 20, Mfuni - who has four caps for England Under-21s - appears to have the best chance of progressing into the senior ranks sooner rather than later.

Fellow 18-year-old Man City centre-back Kaden Braithwaite has not shared as much of the spotlight as Mfuni, yet he remains someone tipped for big things.

Pep Guardiola and Enzo Maresca have both chosen to hand him minutes in the first team, with the latter providing Braithwaite with substitute outings in the Premier League, Champions League and EFL Cup this season.

Unless Man City face EFL opposition in the FA Cup, Braithwaite will not expect to start games this season, but the fact that the nine-cap Under-19 international is already in Maresca's thoughts bodes well for the future.

When West Ham United came back from a three-goal deficit at Cardiff City in Scott Parker's first game in charge, Mayers are one of three half-time introductions and earned widespread praise from the Hammers fanbase.

That subsequently led to a start at left-back three days later in a 2-1 defeat to Blackburn Rovers, but Mayers being immediately promoted by Parker could be the encouragement that the 19-year-old requires to make the step up.

Having made six outings in the Premier League last season, Mayers is now up to 13 appearances for West Ham, and the club's struggles to comply with EFL squad registration rules should lead to the teenager featuring in every Championship squad when fit.

If he can build on the last two games and help West Ham get promoted, the Under-20 international could soon find himself playing regular Premier League football as, presumably, an Under-21 representative for his country.

While Marli Salmon is just 17 years of age, the fact that Mikel Arteta has already handed him three starts and three substitute outings for Arsenal shows the faith that the Spaniard has in the starlet.

Unsurprisingly, Salmon has not always shined in the first team, but completing 90 minutes in a 4-2 win at Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup earlier this season emphasises that there are far more positives than negatives to take at this stage.

A Championship loan may benefit Salmon in the short term, yet it is clear that Arteta views him as a potential long-term member of the Gunners first-team squad.

Furthermore, Salmon is also developing among the best defensive unit in world football, and that can only aid the speed of his progression.

#1799. ‘Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty’ in Hull win as Premier League panel confirm incorrect offside

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel has voted unanimously that Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty against Hull.

The Gunners beat Hull 1-0 in the final match before the international break to go five points clear at the top of the Premier League.

However, it could have been a much more comfortable afternoon had Arsenal been given a penalty in the first half, when it was still goalless.

Kai Havertz went down in the box as he made a run in behind, having been pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

It was not initially seen by the officials but VAR advised the referee to stop play and consult the pitchside monitor.

Farai Hallam deemed that while Havertz had been fouled, he was in an offside position and therefore a free-kick was given to Hull.

The KMI panel have now confirmed that was the incorrect decision due to the foul taking place before Havertz became active.

All five members of the group voted that both the on-field decision and the outcome of the VAR intervention was wrong.

“Although Havertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz,” the panel explained.

“Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded. The panel considered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.”

The panel added: “Being in an offside position, in itself, is not an offence.

“IFAB Law 11 says that a player in an offside position at the moment the ball is played or touched by a team-mate is only penalised on becoming involved in active play.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Graham Potter has hit out at critics of Dejan Kulusevski following the playmaker's cameos for Sweden over the international break.

The 26-year-old subsequently earned a recall to the Sweden team for their Nations League games against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Poland.

Sweden ensured their place at the top of their group by beating Bosnia last week and then drawing 1-1 with Poland on Tuesday. They are now unbeaten in their last 13 Nations League games.

Adrian Benedyczak put Poland ahead in the 16th minute, but Hugo Larsson swiftly equalised for Sweden.

#1797. Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

#1792. Man United transfer news: Monaco open to Balogun sale, but Serie A rival holds an advantage

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 11:51

A Juventus flop wants to leave the Turin club to relaunch his career at Monaco. A swap has been mooted involving Folarin Balogun, who is interested in a move to the Italian side.

A surprising swap has been mooted between Juventus and Monaco. At Juventus, Edon Zhegrova, frustrated at his role as a substitute, wants to leave the Italian club in the January transfer window. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the Kosovan would like to return to Ligue 1.

The former Lille winger has made overtures to Monaco, who need to sign a player in his position this winter, and is pushing for a January transfer.

The 27-year-old right winger has struggled at Juventus. Although he has scored two goals and provided two assists this season, Zhegrova has never been named in the starting line-up by manager Luciano Spalletti.

The Zhegrova situation could be linked to that of Folarin Balogun. The American striker is no longer hiding his desire to leave Monaco, as early as January 2027. His profile appeals to Juventus, who have made signing a centre-forward their priority this winter.

Gazzetta dello Sport therefore reports a possible swap between the Italian club and the Monaco side involving the two players.

Balogun is attracted by the prospect of joining Turin and could push for a transfer to happen. However, the swap is far from agreed, not least because the market values of the two players are quite far apart: €10m (£8.5m) for Zhegrova and €50m (£42.5m) for Balogun.

Juventus also do not appear to want to sign the American permanently. ‘His salary is affordable (around €3.5m a year, or £3m), but it would only become an interesting deal if Monaco agreed to loan him without an option to buy, in order to test him in Serie A before investing between €45m and €50m (£38m-£42.5m)’ - the Italian outlet said. A swap therefore looks unlikely, but two separate deals could well materialise this winter.

Juventus are not the only club said to be keeping tabs on Balogun.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester United are among the clubs to have been approached over a potential move for the forward, with the Red Devils looking to strengthen their attacking options in the winter window.

The report adds that Monaco would be willing to let him leave in January, and that Balogun has been left out of Monaco’s European squad and has made only four Ligue 1 appearances off the bench this season.

A move to Old Trafford could also see Balogun reunited with his former national team manager Mauricio Pochettino, who worked with him with the United States.

Football365 reports that United are hoping to use Pochettino’s relationship with the player, with Fabrizio Romano describing a ‘fantastic connection’ between the two at international level. Romano has also stressed that there is currently ‘no active conversation taking place’, however.

Clearly relishing life under the former Manchester United boss and gaining a reputation for their free-scoring performances in the final third, Madrid will be confident of laying down another title marker.

#1790. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

While the Three Lions were beaten on that occasion, it would be a favourable draw given they have won two of the last three meetings against the Dutch - including the Euro 2024 semi-final.

The simulator hasn't been as kind to France as they've been paired with Spain, a team they have lost to three times in a row since victory in the 2021 final.

In addition, the simulator has thrown up two other eye-catching fixtures with Norway taking on Germany, and Portugal continuing the defence of their crown against Belgium over two legs.

#1789. GdS: Worth the price tag – how Moreira became ‘untouchable’ for Milan and Belgium

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#1788. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners ‘advancing’ on two more contract renewals after Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 12:00

Arsenal are reportedly making progress in contract negotiations for two more first-team stars after Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber.

Following last season's historic Premier League triumph and Champions League final run, the Gunners has spent weeks working behind the scenes to lock down the futures of several key players.

Manager Mikel Arteta committed his future to the Emirates Stadium last month when he put pen to paper on a new-and-improved four-year contract, making him the highest-paid Premier League boss.

Recent reports have claimed that star midfielder Rice has agreed terms over a new five-year deal at Arsenal to keep him in North London until 2031, taking him right through his prime up to the age of 32.

This comes after the England international recently gave an update on his Gunners future, stating that a new deal will "hopefully be arriving soon".

It is also understood that Dutch defender Timber has agreed to sign a new contract with Arsenal that will see him extend his stay beyond the end of his current deal expiring in June 2028.

According to ESPN, Arsenal are now in advanced negotiations to renew the contracts of goalkeeper David Raya and defender Piero Hincapie.

The report adds that both players are ‘very close’ to agreeing fresh terms over extending their current deals at the club.

While Raya was merely a backup for Spain during their triumphant 2026 World Cup campaign, the shot-stopper is an undisputed starter for Arsenal and has grown into a hugely influential figure under Arteta.

Raya, who won his third successive Premier League Golden Glove last season after keeping 19 clean sheets, turned 31 in September and will see his current contract run until 2028.

As for Hincapie, injuries and the form of Riccardo Calafiori have limited the Ecuador international to only three starts and five substitute outings across all competitions so far this season.

However, the 24-year-old remains a key part of Arteta’s plans going forward, with his ability to operate as either a centre-back or left-back making him a valuable asset.

Despite only making his move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent in the summer for around £52m, Hincapie is now in line for an extension beyond 2031.

#1787. Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners, relegation race, Golden Boot and more

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The 2026-27 Premier League season is just days away from resumption following the final international break of the year, and with it the return of some familiar faces.

Mauricio Pochettino is back in English football after a spell in international management, he has succeeded Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach. Meanwhile, Thomas Frank has replaced Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace.

After 10 games of the campaign, both Man United and Palace are in the relegation zone. So will these appointment help to drag them out of the bottom three?

At the other end of the table, Arsenal have made a solid start to the defence of their Premier League crown, and appear to have a surprise challenger as confusion has set in around Manchester City.

Plenty of questions to be answered over the next six months, and the Standard Sport football reporters, Matt Verri, Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau, have had a go at predicting what is in store for the remainder of the season.

MV: Arsenal continue to look ruthlessly efficient and should be confident of defending their title. The defensive unit is absurdly good, the midfield depth is ridiculous, and it means the forwards only need to deliver a moment or two per match.

Even whey they are not at their best, Arsenal are just so difficult to beat. That is the case over 90 minutes and it should be the case over 38 matches again.

DS: No reason to change what I predicted at the beginning of the season, which was for Arsenal to win the Premier League title. If anything, the opening 10 rounds of games have made me more convinced the Gunners won’t be caught and will defend last season’s crown.

Arsenal fans may continue to worry about a lack of goals from their forwards, but their defence is on track to perform even better than last season’s, and that gives other challengers a daunting task to catch them. Arsenal could genuinely win the title by as many as 15 points.

ST: Arsenal were favourites to retain the Premier League title before the season started and that has not changed 10 games in.

MV: Now it gets harder. Liverpool have not quite put it all together yet but there are signs that they will. I’ll go for them to just edge second ahead of Brighton, who have been superb this season but could fade slightly if they go deep in Europe as expected.

Chelsea have the firepower in attack to secure fourth and Unai Emery can work his magic to get Aston Villa into fifth.

DS: My top five, in order, back in August was Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea, then Liverpool. That needs some revising.

Brighton will drop from second but stay strong enough to finish in the Champions League in fourth. Chelsea in fifth — though their performances must improve.

ST: I think the teams who currently occupy the top five spots will all remain there, it is more a case of which position each team will finish. Arsenal will be champions, while I believe Brighton will slip to fifth when the going gets tough in the spring.

Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea are all interchangeable. But I think it will end up being City second, Liverpool third and Chelsea fourth.

MV: Assuming a resolution is reached this season, it is hard to see how Manchester City can avoid a sanction that leads to relegation. I predicted in the summer that Sunderland would go down and that has been reinforced over the first ten games. That squad looks stretched and sorely lacking in goals.

Thomas Frank was abysmal at Tottenham but can do enough to solidify things at Crystal Palace. Instead, Coventry will not quite have enough to stay up.

DS: Along with many others at the time, I predicted the three promoted teams to go straight back down. Even though Hull made a good start, Ipswich have been decent and Coventry seem to have turned a corner, I still expect those three to be weaker than Sunderland, Fulham, Crystal Palace and other strugglers as the many months progress. Coventry, Hull and Ipswich still.

ST: With so much time left in the season, it really is anyone’s guess who will get relegated. Just two points separate the Premier League’s bottom club Crystal Palace and 17th place Coventry, so if Thomas Frank gets it right, the Eagles can quickly pull away from danger.

I think Fulham, Nottingham Forest and Coventry are all capable of getting dragged into the relegation zone.

Sunderland, Forest and Coventry will be the three to go down.

MV: Thierno Barry gets enough chances in front of goal to challenge, while Alexander Isak is starting to show why Liverpool were so determined to sign him. However, it is hard not to be boring. Even with the circus surrounding City, Erling Haaland will almost certainly secure another Golden Boot.

Joao Pedro would be the one I might have backed to challenge him, but injury has stalled his challenge.

DS: Why would it be anyone other than Erling Haaland? It says a lot that even after the Norwegian was criticised in some circles for failing to score in City’s last two league games, the defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest, he is still sitting pretty on top of the leaderboard with nine goals in 10 league games.

The Golden Boot simply won’t be won by anyone else.

ST: It’s the boring answer but in a league lacking natural goalscsorers, Erling Haaland is the obvious pick. The Norwegian has been off the boil in recent weeks, but he always finds his way back into form.

No one knows where the back of the net is quite like Haaland. It’s that simple.

#1786. Pictured: Mauricio Pochettino arrives at airport before starting Manchester United role

Mauricio Pochettino has been pictured arriving in the UK for the first time as Manchester United manager.

The Argentine flew straight from the United States in the early hours of Wednesday morning and the Gulfstream G700 he was believed to be on was spotted landing at Manchester airport shortly before midday.

It was announced last week that the former Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss was making a return to the Premier League, succeeding Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

However, the 54-year-old’s start to his fourth spell in English football was delayed as he finished up commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT), overseeing an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals in his last game in charge.

Now after touching down in the UK, Pochettino can now take the next step in his career.

“I am ready [to return],” he told the Telegraph. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

Pochettino is expected to head to Carrington immediately as he settles into his new role as Man United head coach, with the focus already shifting to his first game in charge against Liverpool on Sunday.

#1785. ‘This is what we dreamed of’ – Pochettino thrilled with USA farewell

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino reflected on a dream ending to his United States tenure as he prepares to take over at Manchester United.

Pochettino was appointed as Man Utd's new head coach last week, but he stayed on to oversee the USA's CONCACAF Nations League two-legged quarter-final tie with Haiti.

The USA romped to a 6-0 win on Saturday, and then followed it up with a routine 2-0 success in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

Pochettino, who took over in 2024, bows out having overseen a six-game unbeaten run since the end of the USA's World Cup campaign.

The USA had 14 shots worth a combined 1.43 expected goals, and enjoyed 74.2% possession. Christian Pulisic scored a stunning overhead kick, while Julian Hall netted his fifth goal in the space of six caps; at 18 years and 238 days old, he is the youngest player ever to net five goals for the USMNT.

"The way we played, that is what we dreamed of when we arrived," Pochettino told reporters.

"When you talk about these games, it looks like it was easy. But Haiti is a World Cup team. The players make the job easier.

"We knew that we have talented players, and in the last six games, being unbeaten and playing against a tough opponent, I see the team really enjoy playing football, playing soccer."

Electric atmosphere @TQLStadium tonight! https://t.co/1e4pIsZnJR

— U.S. Soccer Men's National Team (@USMNT) November 18, 2026

And Pochettino has no doubt that the future is bright for the USA, even if he will not be the coach at the helm.

"I am sure that this group of players, they will achieve big things in the future. I have no doubt," he said.

"[Experienced] players with a mix of younger, with the talent that is coming, I think it's a perfect combination.

"The way that they are leading all the things now, I think it's about being proud of the players, the whole squad, the whole pool of players.

"Of course, it's tough because it's emotional, because I really love these guys and I love the players, I love the staff, I love you, the fans and everything.

"And even if sometimes we have not agreed in our way to see things, that is life, to accept the critics, to accept that someone can disagree with you, with your ideas and see things in a different way. But that is life and you grow through there."

Steve Cherundolo will take charge of the USA's final game of 2026 in December, when they take on Jamaica in a friendly, with a new permanent coach expected to be in place for the CONCACAF Nations League semi-final against Mexico in March.

#1784. Switzerland 4-0 Scotland: Andy Robertson sends stern warning to Sebastien Pocognoli after heavy loss ruins historic night

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 12:05

Scotland captain Andrew Robertson has insisted that new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli does not have time to turn their fortunes around after a heavy 4-0 defeat by Switzerland in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.

It was a bitter sweet night for Robertson at Berit Sitterstadion, as he won his 103rd international cap to become Scotland’s all-time record appearance-maker, surpassing Kenny Dalglish’s record that stood for 40 years.

However, Robertson’s personal achievement was soon overshadowed by a disappointing loss to Switzerland which has consigned them to a third-place finish in League B Group 1 of the Nations League.

Against a much-changed Swiss side, Scotland gifted the hosts a 22nd-minute lead when midfielder Lewis Ferguson inadvertently diverted a harmless cross into his own net.

Scotland’s alarming collapse in St Gallen began with two more goals conceded in the first six minutes of the second half, before Zeki Amdouni netted Switzerland’s fourth in the closing stages to rub salt into the visitors’ wounds.

"I thought first half we were in the game," Robertson told reporters after the match. "We lost a stupid goal but I thought we had chances and could easily have been one-each at half time.

"We talk about it at half time to say keep going and by 50 minutes we're 3-0 down. That cannot happen in international football.

"We were playing against a good team, but we were in the game in the first half. We have to do it for 90 minutes. Then you're 3-0 down at a tough place. A really tough night for us."

Scotland boss Pocognoli, who was appointed as Steve Clarke's successor in August, has previously called for patience as he attempts to implement an attacking philosophy with the national team.

However, the 39-year-old Belgian has prevailed in only two of his first six games in charge – both against North Macedonia – and the Tartan Army have seen their team concede 10 goals in the process.

Questioned on how long it might take for Pocognoli’s approach to yield positive results, Robertson warned: "I don't think you've got time in international football. You have to do it.

"Are those supporters who have travelled everywhere going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No.

“Are the people outside Hampden that are going to be critical, and rightly so, going to give us time? No. We've not got time. The players don't have time. We have to step up.

"We now have a long break until March which is not a good thing. It's going to be a tough one to swallow."

Having accumulated seven points from six Nations League games, Scotland have missed out on a quarter-final spot but have avoided relegation from League B.

Scotland will therefore have no competitive fixtures during the next international break in March 2027 when Pocognoli will instead prepare for friendly fixtures.

#1783. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

#1781. Harry Kane reads letters from his kids: England captain close to tears as his four children write to him after he broke the Three Lions appearance record

Published: 05:47 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:12 EST, 13 November 2026

Harry Kane had to compose himself and hold back the tears while reading beautiful letters from his children after breaking the England appearance record.

The 33-year-old earned his 126th cap and scored in the 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday night, with the Wembley crowd celebrating his achievement and Ballon d'Or triumph.

And on the following morning, there was a surprise in store for the England skipper, who was visibly taken aback on camera when presented with letters from his four children, nine-year-old Ivy, eight-year-old Vivi, five-year-old Louis and three-year-old Henry, who he shares with wife Kate.

'Wow, that’s uh a bit of a surprise,' Kane said as he examined the letters and artwork. 'I think you guys are trying to make me cry on camera.'

He opened the first one before reading aloud: 'To Daddy, I love you very much and I want you to know that I’m very proud of you and also you are the best footballer in the world, the most kind Daddy in the world and the best striker in the world.

'I would like to celebrate you playing the most games for England by holiday together and eating ice cream.

Harry Kane was on the verge of tears as he read touching letters from his four children

'My favorite thing about you is you never give up and I love all things you do for us. Love Ivy.'

Dewy-eyed Kane then reflected: 'I wasn’t expecting this beautiful letter. Thank you Ivy. I love you. I've got one here from Vivian as well.'

'Dear Daddy, I’m so happy and proud of you. I love you because you are hard working and make the best fried eggs. I want to celebrate with you by going fishing, going down the water slides and having a cinema trip as well. Love from Vivi.'

Kane then said: 'Yeah, you’ve caught me by surprise here to be honest with you. I’m trying to just uh, stay strong for the camera. Thank you Vivi, love you.'

Then came the letters from Kane's two sons, Louis and Henry.

Louis' read: 'To Daddy, I love you so much because you train and work so hard. My favorite thing we do together is play football and cricket together. I love when you play England football because you score goals and we get to sing Vindaloo. I want to celebrate with you by making an ice cream house with sweets inside. Love Louis.'

'Thank you Louie, love you, boy. This last one is from Henry,' Kane said.

The short and sweet note from his youngest went: 'Daddy, you are the winner. Vindaloo! Love Henry.'

Kane walked onto the pitch with his children, (L-R) Henry, Ivy, Vivi, Louis on Thursday night

Kane showed the artwork and hand-written letters to the camera as he read them

Kane then pointed the endearing scribble to the camera, saying: 'He’s drawn me a lovely picture there. Love you, Henry. Thank you, beautiful messages from my wonderful family.'

Kane, who lives with his family in Bavaria and recently signed a new deal worth £400,000-a-week at Bayern Munich, brought the whole clan, including his parents, to Wembley for his big night on Thursday.

He walked out onto the hallowed turf with his four children, admired a gigantic tifo of himself in the crowd, posed for pictures with the gleaming Ballon d'Or trophy and was given a commemorative shirt by Prince William.

Kane is a devoted family man in addition to being the world's best footballer and took a moment to say a few words about his children at the Ballon d'Or ceremony last month.

He said: 'To Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

Prince William presented Kane with a commemorative framed shirt with 126 on the back

'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'

Kane passed Peter Shilton as the record appearance-maker for England on Thursday and took his tally of goals for the national team to 92.

His penalty put England 2-1 up and they would not relinquish their lead. He'll next be in action against Spain on Sunday.

#1780. Manchester United urged to target ‘established Premier League leader’ as Bruno Fernandes replacement

Former Manchester United winger Ashley Young has revealed he would replace Bruno Fernandes with Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Fernandes's contract expires at the end of this season, though United can extend their captain’s deal by an additional year and also prevent him from speaking to foreign clubs in January about a potential free transfer.

United want Fernandes to stay, but the 32-year-old has already turned down two new contract proposals as he weighs up his options following more managerial turnover at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his first training session on Wednesday after leaving the US men’s national team to replace Michael Carrick as United head coach.

Fernandes enjoyed a superb campaign last term, breaking the single-season Premier League assist record to help United qualify for the Champions League.

This season, however, he has struggled to replicate the same form, and he drew criticism after calling into question Carrick’s tactics following United’s 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como in October.

While Young admits there is no doubt about Fernandes’ contribution to United, with the Portuguese midfielder producing 75 goals and 74 assists in 239 Premier League appearances, he insists that in order for the Red Devils to move on, they should look to replace the former Sporting man with England international Gibbs-White.

“Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young tells Standard Sport.

“There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White.

“I think he's got 18 months left on his contract. He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”

#1779. Chelsea and Manchester United lead tributes as Juan Mata announces football retirement

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea and Manchester United led the tributes to Juan Mata after he announced his retirement from professional football.

The former Spain international, who lifted the 2010 World Cup and 2012 European Championship, has hung up his boots at the age of 38 after leaving Australian giants Melbourne Victory in September.

Mata started his career at Real Madrid’s academy before moving to Valencia in 2007, where he won the 2008 Copa del Rey alongside fellow future World Cup winners David Silva and David Villa.

He moved to Chelsea in 2011 and helped the Blues win the Champions League and FA Cup in his first season at the club. The diminutive midfielder was crowned Chelsea’s Player of the Year in both of his two full seasons in west London before leaving for Manchester United in January 2014.

Mata helped United win the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup before his departure in 2022. He then spent the latter years of his career with Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

Mata announced his retirement with a 50-second video posted on his social media channels.

In the video, Mata sits in a changing room, staring at a pair of football boots. He then turns around and hangs them up on a peg, with the caption: “Sometimes to love is to let go. Thanks, football.”

A full statement was also posted on Mata’s official website, in which he admitted “Football will never leave my life” and that he would continue to use football “as a vehicle for development.”

Mata is best known for co-founding Common Goal, a global movement in which players, coaches, and clubs pledge at least 1% of their salaries to fund grassroots football charities.

“I was able to keep going for so many years because of the sheer joy of playing. Waking up every morning looking forward to training and playing, whether at magnificent grounds such as Old Trafford, Stamford Bridge or Mestalla.

“Or back when I was starting out at Juventud Estadio, where the pitch turned into a mud bath every winter. I believe that kind of passion is fundamental to everything in life.

“Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.”

Manchester United paid tribute to Mata, who scored 51 goals in 285 games for the Red Devils, with a post on social media.

“Great player, better person. Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan,” they wrote on social media.

Chelsea also posted a tribute to Mata on their social media pages.

“What a player,” Chelsea wrote in response to his retirement announcement.

#1778. Vinicius Junior: Real Madrid star reveals impact of Arsenal transfer speculation with honest admission

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 12:10, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 12:10

Vinicius Junior has admitted that feeling “truly overwhelmed” by summer transfer speculation is partly to blame for his slow start to the season at Real Madrid.

The 26-year-old was allegedly targeted by Premier League champions Arsenal who were keen to explore a big-money move for the left-sided attacker as he approached the final 12 months of his contract.

However, a transfer to the Emirates Stadium failed to materialise and Vinicius opted to sign a new long-term contract at Real Madrid in August, keeping him at the Bernabeu until 2032.

Speculation over his future in the Spanish capital intensified shortly after Brazil's disappointing last-16 exit at the 2026 World Cup, which led to him not training as much as he should have by his own admission.

Under new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, Vinicius has been unable to reach the heights expected on a consistent basis, scoring just one goal and registering three assists in 12 appearances across all competitions this season.

Vinicius has since opened up on how a summer of speculation and an early World Cup exit has contributed to his drop-off in form at club level.

“I don’t think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians,” Vinicius said at a press conference in Singapore ahead of Brazil’s friendly on Tuesday.

“Being knocked out so early was something we hadn’t expected, so I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family.

“I ended up training less than in previous years. That may have affected my start to the season.

“On ‌top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid, but it’s a very long season.”

In October, Vinicius was handed a straight red card and a four-match suspension after pulling the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba.

Real Madrid’s club-record signing Yan Diomande has since flourished for Mourinho’s side in Vinicius’s preferred left-sided position, and the Brazilian has acknowledged that he has work to do to win back his place in the starting lineup.

“Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult,” Real’s No.7 added.

“I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and [Lionel] Messi have managed to do this for so many years, reaching the same kinds of numbers. I am human, I often make mistakes, but I always try to improve.”

Since joining Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018, Vinicius has played 387 times for the club across all competitions, recording 129 goals and 103 assists as well as winning three La Liga titles and two Champions Leagues.

Mourinho recently stated that he is confident that Vinicius will rediscover his top form with the Spanish giants in the not too distant future.

#1777. England’s Ivan Toney fails in bid to move assault trial over Euro 2028 clash

Get our award-winning daily news email featuring exclusive stories, opinion and expert analysis

Ivan Toney’s bid to move the date of his assault trial to avoid clashing with Euro 2028 games has been refused by a judge.

The England footballer, 30, hopes to be selected to play for the national side in the next European Championship after featuring in this summer’s World Cup .

Toney is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on December 6, 2025.

He denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a three- to four-day trial was fixed for June 12, 2028, which is three days into the Uefa Euro 2028 tournament.

At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, which Toney did not attend, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: “It came to our attention that… there may be potentially a football match called the European championships in 2028 between June 9 and July 9.”

Mr Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: “We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.

“My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup.”

Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a “speculative” application.

He refused the request, saying: “It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed.”

The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.

An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Mr Da Silva.

It was heard the two men “squared up to each other”, before Toney allegedly “lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches”.

The Metropolitan Police investigated and the footballer was charged in late July.

Toney, of Northampton, has made 10 international appearances and scored one goal.

He missed out on the latest squad for the country’s Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

#1776. Pickford still England’s number one over Trafford, claims Young

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jordan Pickford should still get the nod as England's number one goalkeeper over James Trafford, so says Ashley Young.

Thomas Tuchel has used this Nations League campaign to split time evenly between Pickford and Trafford.

Pickford has been England's undisputed number one since 2017, with the 32-year-old making 94 appearances and keeping 49 clean sheets.

Peter Shilton (125) is the only goalkeeper to have won more caps for England than Pickford, though he now has fierce competition from Leeds United shot-stopper Trafford, who made a string of fine saves to help the Three Lions beat Spain on Sunday.

Pickford has now not started four of England's last seven competitive internationals, having only not been in the XI for two of their previous 41 beforehand.

However, in their last nine competitive matches without Jordan Pickford, England have only kept two clean sheets and conceded an average of two goals per game (18 in total).

And even though Trafford's performance saw plenty of calls for the 24-year-old to be installed as England's first-choice goalkeeper, Young has backed his former Everton club-mate Pickford.

"You've always got to give goalkeepers the chance to show what they're about," Young said on The Overlap Daily.

"Playing as a defender, you want to know who's behind you as a goalkeeper. Right, that's it, this is who's going to be our number one. That's who’s going to be in goal. And I think, rightly so, Jordan Pickford has earned 94 caps for a reason.

"I'm more confident in Pickford than Trafford with his feet. But when you've got different managers, it's different. At Everton, they play out from the back at times but not as much as England do. For me, Pickford's England's number one."

Blackburn Rovers have announced that head coach Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his position due to health issues.

Mowbray was appointed as the replacement for Michael O'Neill in the summer and has subsequently guided Rovers to 13th place in the Championship table.

The 62-year-old had taken on his second managerial role - the other coming at West Bromwich Albion - since previously taking time away from football for health reasons in 2024.

"I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Shaikh, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

The international break has played out something like an Oprah Winfrey show for the Arsenal squad.

Oprah, back in 2004, marched around her studio, declaring all those in the audience had won a car. Just the 276 Pontiac G6s dished out, for those wondering.

Andrea Berta has seemingly been following that example at Arsenal. “You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!”

It started with the news that Declan Rice had reached an agreement over a new long-term deal, one that will see him join Bukayo Saka on around £350,000-a-week.

Jurrien Timber, too, is set to commit his future to the club. Like Rice, he had entered the final two years of his current deal but the intention was always for Arsenal to tie him down beyond that.

There was more. David Raya has agreed fresh terms as well and will sign a new contract, a year on from receiving a pay rise. This deal will keep him at Arsenal through to 2030.

Piero Hincapie wanted in and is understood to have joined the extension club. The defender only signed for the Gunners permanently in the summer and that deal did not expire until 2031.

However, Hincapie has been rewarded with improved terms for his contribution to the title-winning season and a 12-month extension on the previous deal.

A busy period, then, for those involved in the building and managing of this squad. An extremely indicative one, too, both of how far Arsenal have come and where they want to get to.

It was not that long ago that contract negotiations for key players were a major source of stress for the club.

Under Arsene Wenger, Alexis Sanchez made it clear he had no desire to sign a new deal. Arsenal decided not to sell and he went into the last year of his contract, before joining Manchester United in a swap deal with Henrikh Mkhitaryan.

Terrified of losing Mesut Ozil for free and having been dragged into the final six months of his deal in 2018, Arsenal threw the kitchen sink at him and gave him a £350,000-a-week deal.

For years, Arsenal fans knew exactly when the contracts of the most important players would run out, almost fearing the two years leading up to that.

Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners and more

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal in Vinicius talks; Man Utd deal confirmed

Arsenal get new Havertz penalty review as Premier League panel confirm error

Not so now. Rice has entered the final 18 months of his existing deal but there was no real sense of jeopardy. The assumption was always that an extension would be agreed and that has proved correct.

This is now a club that players want to sign but just as crucially want to stay at. Rice’s new deal will commit his prime years to the club, as will be the case with Raya.

You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!

Had Rice wished to explore his options elsewhere, he would have had his pick of the elite clubs across Europe, as would William Saliba before he signed a new deal last year.

Arsenal might not be able to sign the most high-profile players from clubs like Real Madrid, as the summer pursuit of Vinicius Junior showed, but they can now protect their own assets regardless of who wants them.

There are still decisions to be made over other situations. Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz are both out of contract in 2028 as it stands. So too is Ben White and it is understood that as with Odegaard, no contract talks have yet taken place with the club.

However, the dynamic is very different to the one Arsenal have had to put up with in the past. These are not desperate negotiations. If these are players are leave in the transfer windows ahead, it feels like that would be a club-led decision.

These contract extensions also point to the power Mikel Arteta has and the priorities of the club. This is not about building a squad for five or six years down the line. Everything is centred towards giving Arteta the tools to win immediately.

That was apparent in the summer signings of Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes, both now 29, and in the handing out of huge contracts to take players well into their 30s.

Arteta has signed a contract of his own through to 2030 and it is all about maximising every opportunity for major trophies between now and then.

His priority is this season and the three beyond it. What happens after that, in terms of the age profile of the squad or the contract situations in the squad, might not be Arteta’s problem.

By then he might be driving off into the sunset. Probably not in a Pontiac G6.
